rules.title: One compiled data file
rules.interpretation: A Node script compiles the trail into a versioned `trace.json` at build time. The SPA reads only that file: no runtime reads of the repo, no server

tests.name: npm run trace compiles a trail into one versioned trace.json, and the activity chunk it names
the app shows the trail it is served as trace.json, and fetches nothing from the repo or a server
compile writes trace.json under src/Uinsure.Policies.Web/public/, at schemaVersion 1.0.0
trace.json holds exactly the v1.0.0 index fields, each list a list
a clean trail compiles with no problem listed
the plan, its node and its rules come from the plan DAG and the requirements
the node's commits are read from their trailers, field by field
events hold the complete trail's nine loop lines, and rule status stays null with no matrix to drive it
trace.json names build/F1's activity chunk, and every chunk it names is written beside it
the compiler writes trace.json and the chunks it names, and nothing else
the activity chunk holds the node's activity, one entry per line, in order
the loader reads the compiled trace.json and hands over what it holds
the loader makes one request, for trace.json beside the app, and no other
a trace.json of the same major version (1.4.0) is read
a trace.json of the next major version (2.0.0) is refused, naming its version
a trace.json of an earlier major version (0.9.0) is refused, naming its version
a trace.json with no schemaVersion is refused
no trace.json (404) is an error naming trace.json, never an empty trace
a trace.json that is not JSON is an error, never an empty trace
while the dev server answers trace.json "compiling" (503, X-Docket-Trace: compiling), the loader asks again and settles ready on the compiled file
the "did not compile" 503 (X-Docket-Trace: failed) is final: an error after exactly one request
a 503 that says "compiling" only in its prose, with no X-Docket-Trace marker, is final: an error after exactly one request
a fetch that fails outright settles as an error, not a rejection
a node's activity is read from the chunk trace.json names, record by record
reading a node's activity makes one request, for its chunk beside the app
a node whose chunk trace.json names as null has no activity, and nothing is fetched
a node trace.json does not hold is an error, and nothing is fetched
a chunk the host doesn't have (404) is an error, never an empty activity
a chunk that is not a JSON array is an error, never an empty activity
on a clone with no node_modules, the F5 web target restores packages or stops naming npm ci, never "Cannot find module"
on a clone with no node_modules and npm offline, the esproj StartupCommand run as written names npm ci, with no registry fetch and never "Cannot find module"
the dev server answers on its port while the trail compiles: /trace.json says it is compiling, then serves the compiled trail
under vite preview a failed compile is reported on the console and /trace.json answers 503, or preview compiles nothing
package.json declares the Node minimum in engines, and .nvmrc names the same version, at least 22.22
a fresh tree started with npx vite serves /trace.json, compiled from the trail at its HEAD

plans.hypothesis:
The orchestrator's fix brief for the QA what-if defect specified "two jobs in one stage", on a wrong model of

plans.title: What main still holds after #121
plans.question: Does main, after #121, still hold unfinished or defective work (a plan node not done, a carry-over or deferred finding that no node closes, a first-run gap where a fresh clone can't F5 straight into Docket, a Docket region still marked "not built yet", or a workbench interaction that doesn't show the request it sent and the response it got), and if so which items?
plans.hypothesis:
Yes, in four groups:
- **(a) First run.** Nothing in the VS launch path restores `node_modules` or opens Docket, and the trace compile blocks Vite's start.
- **(b) Placeholders.** The "request as sent" inspector regions on Sell and Cancel were never given to a node.
- **(c) Workbench defects.** The Send result is read from a field the screen's data doesn't hold, the JSON is printed without indentation, and the request view is cleared after sending.
- **(d) Plan state.** No commit moved F7, F8 or U10 to done.

Each part is disproved by code on main that already does the thing, or by DAG statuses that already read done:
- an npm restore in the launch path, or a launch that opens Docket
- a built inspector region
- a Status bound to the response
- indented JSON

plans.hypothesis: Listen-first (35122e4b) moved "ready" from port-bind to compile-end, but Vite's --open fires on listen, not on printUrls, and the shell loads trace.json once and treats a 503 as terminal; no test drives a page against the dev server during the compile. plans.question: Why does bug-002/N2 FAIL the e2e gate at attempt 2 (wb-sell's receipt heading "Receipt for rung 4: what was sent, what came back" is in the DOM but covered by the sticky requests drawer in the regression screenshots), and is the cause in the sell screen's region composition, in the kit drawer's sticky docking, or in tests that check the heading exists but not that it is visible?

findings.what: PolicyService.Details works out the current term and the Pending/Expired/Active status itself. F1 never reads Status, and no test covers those branches.
findings.why: The code-quality skill says PolicyService orchestrates and holds no rules. signatures.md puts Policy.CurrentTerm(today) and Policy.StatusOn(today), plus LatestTerm, in the domain. The GET-1 and Status rows of requirements.md are rules. This logic arrived in the t10 api green commit without a red test (gate.green loop.jsonl:29 says 'Pending/Active/Expired status are F2 scope'). Grep shows PolicyDetails.Status is never read in src/Uinsure.Policies.Api, so in F1 these are untested and unused branches, and they also miss the Cancelled case. Either put this in the domain with red tests, or leave it to F2 and return the trivial single-term value for now.

findings.what: No test shows a duplicate reference returns the 409 alone when its body also breaks a 422 rule. The service's duplicate check has no Services.Tests red test.
findings.why: requirements.md §2 Response standard says a 409 short-circuits before the rules are evaluated. api.md Evaluation order says each 409 short-circuits on its own. architecture says SELL-1 is checked in the service via GetByReference. Every duplicate test posts an otherwise valid body, so swapping the check and Policy.Sell in PolicyService.Sell would still pass. tdd-outside-in step 4 asks for red Services.Tests wherever Services has logic. This check arrived in the t10 api green commit with no Services red test (gate.green loop.jsonl:29 says so). RecordingPolicyRepository already supports such a test.

findings.what: No test covers the index-backed 409. The step from a unique-violation DbUpdateException (SQLite 2067, SQL Server 2601/2627) to PersistenceConflictException to SELL-1 409 is unverified.
findings.why: The SELL-1 agreed interpretation says 'A unique DB index enforces it too'. The architecture HTTP-edge table says PersistenceConflictException(DuplicateReference) gives a 409 'as SELL-1'. A search of tests/ finds no PersistenceConflict, DuplicateReference or concurrency test. If the error-code filter were wrong, a racing duplicate would get a 500, and the suite would not notice. The race can be forced in Api.Tests, for example with a test-only repository whose GetByReference skips the service check.

findings.what: The race-path SELL-1 409 has no 'reference' extension and a different detail from the service path. It is built in UnexpectedExceptionHandler, not through ResultExtensions.
findings.why: The api.md matrix row for SELL-1 lists the extension 'reference' and the detail form 'A policy with reference ... already exists.' The architecture says DuplicateReference answers 'as SELL-1' and that ResultExtensions builds the response in one place. Here the same rule has two bodies that differ, and the status is hard-coded outside ProblemCatalog.StatusFor. A handler named 'Unexpected' now also handles an expected conflict.

findings.what: Policyholders and Terms are auto-included with no ordering by key. The read-back holder order and termNumber (index + 1) depend on the order the provider returns rows.
findings.why: The SELL-4 tests assert that policyholders read back in the order sold, and SELL-5's 'index' is a 1-based position. PolicyMappings numbers terms by list position. EF Core does not document an order for collection navigations without an explicit ordering, and SQL Server, the migration target, may return rows in another order than SQLite. Green on SQLite today, but fragile.

findings.what: firstName, lastName and addressLine1-3 have no max length on the DTO, but the EF columns cap them at 100 and 200. Only postcode has [MaxLength(8)].
findings.why: API4 row: string max lengths must be on both the DTO and the EF column. The EF columns are HasMaxLength(100/200) and the DTO has nothing, so overlong input is not a 400. On SQL Server (the evidence target) it fails at SaveChanges as a truncation DbUpdateException, which is not a unique violation, so the client gets a 500. On SQLite (the runtime) HasMaxLength is not enforced, so strings up to the 64 KB body limit are stored and echoed back. The Domain tests have no case for this.

findings.what: DateOfBirth.AddYears(16) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a dateOfBirth of year 9984 or later. The request becomes a generic 500 logged at Error.
findings.why: Client-controlled input reaches an unguarded date calculation. No body or stack trace leaks, but the client can force 500s and Error log noise, which is an availability and hygiene weakness. Guard the add (for example by comparing against start.AddYears(-16)), or reject implausible dates of birth. No test covers the extreme date.

findings.what: Amount below about -7.9e26 (e.g. -1000000000000000000000000000) makes amount * 100 overflow in Validate: OverflowException, then a 500 logged at Error instead of 422 SELL-7.
findings.why: The guard 'amount > MaxAmount' only stops overflow for positive values, though the comment says the limit check keeps * 100 from overflowing. A large negative decimal binds under strict JSON, reaches IValidatableObject.Validate and throws. UnexpectedExceptionHandler then answers a generic 500 at LogError. In F1 the same body got 422 SELL-7 (amount <= 0), so this breaks the F1b acceptance 'No behaviour change' and the HTTP-edge contract: client input must never cause a 500.

findings.what: The amount shape rows test only the positive side (2dp, 3dp, 0.001, 1,000,000.00, 1,000,000.01). No row sells an extreme negative amount, so the R1 overflow path is untested.
findings.why: Requirements-trace: each side of a boundary is its own test, and a test written from a finding must fail before the fix commit. The H6 shape check has a scale limit on both signs, and the SELL-7 failure row (amount <= 0) needs an extreme-negative case that asserts 422 SELL-7 (or 400 if David rules it shape), never 500.

findings.what: ReferenceGenerator keeps public static Payment() next to the explicit IReferenceGenerator.Payment(). The static is a second way around the injected seam; only ReferenceGeneratorTests call it.
findings.why: Code-quality: DI at the layer seams (IReferenceGenerator), with no dead or duplicate surface. Task t6 kept the static calls only for the stub. After the t8 green, PolicyService uses the interface, so the static is a leftover that lets later code bypass the seam the A15 test asserts.

findings.what: Domain.Tests for LatestTerm, CurrentTerm and StatusOn use only one-term policies. A LatestTerm => Terms[0] mutation survives every Domain test; only Services.Tests (two terms via Restore) kill it.
findings.why: Requirements-trace: rule logic is proven at every boundary in Domain.Tests. The F1b acceptance says these members 'live in the Domain with Domain.Tests'. Before F2 adds the GET-1 traits, a two-term Domain test should prove LatestTerm is the last term and that StatusOn measures Expired from it.

findings.what: Amount check overflows on a large negative amount: amount * 100 throws OverflowException inside Validate, so the client gets a 500 and an Error log instead of the SELL-7 422.
findings.why: The check only bounds the positive side (amount > MaxAmount). A JSON amount such as -1000000000000000000000000000 parses as a decimal, passes the limit test, and then amount * 100 exceeds decimal.MaxValue. Any caller can trigger an unhandled exception on demand. The comment 'Checking the limit first keeps * 100 from overflowing' is wrong for negatives. The node's own acceptance says nothing ambiguous reaches the domain, and SELL-7 says a negative amount is 422. SellAmountShapeTests has no large-negative row.

findings.what: hasClaims is hard-coded false in ToResponse, though Policy.HasClaims is stored and restored. No test seeds true, so a canned stub passes every hasClaims assertion.
findings.why: GET-1 returns the stored policy, and the F2 acceptance asks for the full response shape per api.md. Policy.HasClaims already exists end to end: PolicyRecord.HasClaims, PolicyRecordMapper.cs:21 into Policy.Restore, and PolicyRepository.cs:70. The comment says it is canned 'until F3 supplies the data', but that data is supplied today, so a canned stub value is left in green production code. The anti-oracle rule is broken too. PolicyResponseAssert.HasNoClaimsRefundsOrCancellation only ever expects false, and the Api.Tests PolicyBuilder passes a literal false to Restore with no override, so no test can tell the canned value from the stored one. A red test that seeds HasClaims=true and reads it back over HTTP must come before the mapping fix. Refunds, claims and cancellation have no domain data yet, so they are rightly canned.

findings.what: Header comment still says status and currentTermNumber are 'canned for now (stub step)'. At HEAD both come from PolicyDetails.Status and the current term's index.
findings.why: This is on the code-quality slop list: a comment that is false at HEAD. The refactor step fixed the same kind of stale comment on TwoDecimalPlacesConverter (7023420, 803c898) but missed this one. PolicyMappings.cs:23 already lists what is still canned.

findings.what: Global decimal converter writes with "F2", a silent second rounding path beside Money.Round. Its 'no >2 dp value reaches it' invariant lives only in a comment.
findings.why: CLAUDE.md says to round money only through Money.Round. At HEAD the invariant holds: the H6 400 rejects more than 2 dp by value before any 422 echo, and stored amounts come only from accepted sales. But F3's refunds will go through this converter, and "F2" formatting would hide a missing or wrong Money.Round (CANCEL-6) in every Api test. The change to problem echoes (-1e27 now written -1000000000000000000000000000.00) is consistent with the api.md money convention, but only gate.run evidences it. No Api test pins the echo's text, and the Postman decimal.MinValue test's include('"amount":-79228162514264337593543950335') is a prefix match that passes with or without '.00'.

findings.what: Known keys are every action parameter name, so ?reference= and ?cancellationToken= on GET (and ?request= on POST) pass without a 400, though no query value binds to them.
findings.why: The architecture skill says 'an unbound query key (case-insensitive) gives errors[key]', and requirements say an unknown query parameter returns 400. Route-bound, body-bound and special parameters are counted as known query keys. The only test is ?colour=red.

findings.what: Unpaid_second_term_reads_back_with_no_payment_reference_and_no_payment never asserts status, so its read-back is not full. Active is expected on 2026-10-17.
findings.why: The tdd-outside-in skill requires a full read-back of every field the node's response carries, and status is a GET-1 field. The row is stub-proof now only through currentTermNumber (canned 0 vs 1). A status literal would pin it on a second derived value, as the other rows in this class do.

findings.what: No Services test covers PolicyService.Get's not-found branch (NotFound kind, GET-1 id, detail, reference extension). It is proven over HTTP only.
findings.why: The tdd-outside-in skill wants Services.Tests where Services has logic, and PolicyService.cs:57-63 builds the GET-1 violation. RuleCoverageTests passes because unit traits exist, so this does not block coverage. But GET-1's failure row has no unit-level test. The orchestrator recorded this gap in gate.green at 311ccb6.

findings.what: Quote action calls service.Get then service.QuoteCancellation: two loads and two UK-today reads per request; quotedOn and the CANCEL-3 check can disagree across midnight.
findings.why: api.md Conventions: 'Today is UkCalendar.Today(TimeProvider), Europe/London, computed once per request.' quotedOn comes from Get's today (PolicyDetails.Today, a member added beyond the binding signatures.md PolicyDetails(Policy, CurrentTerm, Status)), while the default date and the CANCEL-3 past-date check use a second today read inside QuoteCancellation. PolicyServiceQuoteTests.Quote_reads_the_clock_once proves one read per service call, not per request.

findings.what: PolicyMappings.ToQuote re-implements Policy.Cancel rules in the Api: top-level rule from CurrentTerm and refunds only for a paid term above 0 (no £0 refund).
findings.why: code-quality: 'Rules live in the domain. Controllers map HTTP to the service and back.' COULD-1: 'A read-only version of the cancel calculation'. The refund-eligibility rule (requirements 'No £0 refunds' / CANCEL-2) and the top-level ruleApplied choice now exist both in Policy.Cancel (Policy.cs) and in this mapping. They agree today (CancellationQuoteTests.Quote_and_a_later_cancel_for_the_same_date_agree), but a change to one won't reach the other.

findings.what: RecordClaim action re-reads the policy after saving and treats the last claim as the new one; a concurrent claim in between is returned instead, and stored.Value is unchecked.
findings.why: The service already returns the recorded Claim, but the action does a second load (and a second UK-today read) to find the claim number from Claims.Count. Another claim saved between the two calls would make E5 return that claim's reference, date and description (api.md E5 ClaimResponse). If the re-read fails, stored.Value throws and the request becomes a 500 instead of a ProblemDetails.

findings.what: Policy.Restore gained optional claims/cancellation defaults that only test builders use; signatures.md makes both required and the one src caller passes both.
findings.why: signatures.md (binding): Restore(..., IReadOnlyList<Claim> claims, Cancellation? cancellation). The only src caller (PolicyRecordMapper.cs:18) passes both. The '= null' defaults serve only Domain/Services/Api test builders that omit them. code-quality slop list: speculative generality, and a production signature bent for tests.

findings.what: RecordClaim re-reads the policy after saving and answers with the last claim, so a concurrent claim could be returned as this caller's claim.
findings.why: Hygiene, not an integrity break. The Version token (PolicyRepository.SaveChanges) rejects a concurrent write on the same policy with 409, and the claim is stored correctly. Only the 201 body's claim number could point at another request's claim in a narrow window. Not blocking.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: managed identity to Entra-only SQL
findings.what: Pipeline runs CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER as a service principal, but the SQL server has no identity with Graph/Directory Readers rights, so the grant step fails
findings.why: This acceptance line needs the app's managed identity to reach Entra-only SQL. The pipeline signs in as the service-connection principal (stage-template.yml line 90) and runs CREATE USER [$(appName)] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER. When a service principal runs that statement, Azure SQL looks up the name in Microsoft Graph using the logical server's own identity. That identity needs User.Read.All, GroupMember.Read.All and Application.Read.All, or the Directory Readers role. sql.bicep gives the server no identity block, and neither the template nor its comments name the prerequisite. As written, the first deploy to any environment fails at the 'Grant the app's managed identity database access' step, and the app's identity never gets a database user. checker and bicep build only test the text, so neither can catch this. David must be able to defend this line, and an Azure reviewer will ask about this exact step.

findings.what: dotnet-ef is installed globally with no version, so the migration script's tool version depends on the day the pipeline runs
findings.why: This is the dotnet-ef pinning carry-over (9.0.9 vs runtime 10.0.13), which every snapshot from F0b to F4 assigned to F5 (docs/qa/build-F0b.md step 18 note). The pipeline now repeats the problem: the version of the idempotent script's generator is not reproducible, and it can drift from EF Core 10.0.13 in Directory.Packages.props. pre-push uses `dotnet tool restore`, but the repo has no tool manifest.

findings.what: Output principalId is declared but never consumed by main.bicep or the pipeline
findings.why: This is on the slop list as an unused member. The grant step looks the identity up by appName, so nothing reads principalId.

findings.what: tenantId is a parameter with a zero-GUID placeholder in all three param files and a pipeline override, though a subscription deployment already knows its tenant
findings.why: tenant().tenantId is available at subscription scope. The parameter adds a placeholder per environment, a variable-group entry and an override argument to the what-if and create commands, and no rule needs any of them.

findings.what: SQL server has publicNetworkAccess Enabled plus the AllowAzureServices 0.0.0.0 rule, so any Azure-hosted caller can reach port 1433.
findings.why: Network exposure hardening. Entra-only auth and TLS 1.2 limit the risk, so it is not exploitable on its own. A private endpoint or the app's outbound IPs would shrink the surface. The 'evidence only, never deployed' scope makes this non-blocking.

findings.what: Basic-auth publishing credentials for SCM/Kudu (and FTP) are not disabled; only ftpsState is Disabled.
findings.why: Least privilege and misconfiguration. The pipeline deploys with az webapp deploy through the service connection and doesn't need basic auth. Add basicPublishingCredentialsPolicies for scm and ftp with allow=false.

findings.what: The deployment service principal is a member of the SQL admin group and runs migrations and user grants as admin, in every environment including prod.
findings.why: Least privilege. The app's own identity is correctly limited to db_datareader and db_datawriter, so it holds no DDL rights. The pipeline identity is a standing SQL admin, and the design should record that as an accepted trade-off.

findings.what: dotnet-ef is installed as a global tool with no version pin, and the agent image is ubuntu-latest, so a floating tool version runs in the build that produces the prod migration script.
findings.why: Pipeline supply-chain hygiene. Pin the tool version (--version, or a tool manifest) so the packages are reproducible and approved.

findings.what: fix commits 2c0b4e7 and 4012f0e carry no Fixes-Finding trailer, so no trailer links the A1 fixes to I1-I8
findings.why: The requirements-trace skill says every fix(...) commit carries Fixes-Finding. The commit-msg hook accepts the round form A1/I1 (lines 27-29), so G9 did not block this. 2c0b4e7 should name A1/I1 to A1/I8. 4012f0e fixes a gate observation, not a finding, so its fix( prefix has no finding to cite. Because the trailer is missing, the trail links a fix to its finding only through the commit body text.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: AzureCLI@2 deploy; managed identity to Entra-only SQL
findings.what: The SQL steps set azureSubscription: $(sqlServiceConnection) from a job-level variable group; service connections must resolve when the pipeline compiles, so this may fail resource authorization
findings.why: Azure DevOps authorizes service connections before the run, and a macro variable that resolves at runtime is a known cause of 'service connection could not be found'. I can't confirm from here whether a job-level variable group resolves in time, and it was never run (az and DevOps were never used). The ARM connection already uses a compile-time template parameter (azureServiceConnection). A second template parameter would remove the risk, and the checker's I8 assertion would still pass. Please have the investigator verify this before David has to defend it.

findings.what: The I5 pool check only requires that 'vmImage' is absent, so a deployment job with its pool deleted (the default Microsoft-hosted pool) still passes
findings.why: The assertion is meant to prove that the SQL steps run inside the network. All it rejects is an explicit vmImage key. Asserting that pool.name is present (for example, the policies-<env>-vnet pattern) would stop a mutant without a pool from passing. The infrastructure at HEAD is correct (pool.name is set). The gap is the oracle's strength.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: no secrets / least privilege (I8 trade-off text)
findings.what: The comment says 'a leaked pipeline token cannot administer the server', but the ARM service connection in the same job can rewrite the server's Entra admin through ARM
findings.why: A subscription-scope deployment needs Contributor-level rights, and with them it can write Microsoft.Sql/servers administrators. The split does keep the SQL connection to database scope, which is a real gain. But the sentence as written claims more than that, and an Azure reviewer will challenge it. Scope the claim to the SQL service connection's token, or name the ARM path as an accepted residual risk. Code-quality rule: comments must be explainable and true.

findings.what: Neither subnet has an NSG, so the SQL private endpoint on 1433 is reachable from the whole VNet and from any network peered to it (the self-hosted agent network).
findings.why: Network hardening. SQL is Entra-only and has no public endpoint, so this is not exploitable by itself. An NSG on the integration subnet, with privateEndpointNetworkPolicies enabled on the endpoint subnet, would allow 1433 only from the app subnet and the agent range. Non-blocking for evidence-only IaC.

findings.what: The S1 deny and allow-1433 checks scan all of network.bicep. If the private-endpoint NSG's deny-all is deleted, the checker still passes on the app NSG's deny-all
findings.why: This is the same weakness A2 R3 found in I5. The deny regex at lines 179-180 and the 1433/Allow checks at lines 177-178 aren't tied to the NSG on snet-private-endpoints. Take the mutant with the deny-all-inbound rule removed from privateEndpointNsg. Default AllowVnetInBound would then let the whole VNet and any peered network reach 1433, which is exactly the S1 exposure. The checker still passes because appIntegrationNsg matches 'direction Inbound ... access Deny'. The message 'the SQL NSG must deny all other inbound traffic' claims more than the check proves. The infrastructure at HEAD is correct. The gap is in the oracle. gate.pipeline-schema@c4032df names a mutant for R3 only, none for S1.

findings.rule_id: code-quality: comments must be true and explainable
findings.what: 'The agent's network also needs to be allowed by the pool' is unclear and out of date. Since S1, the agents must fall inside agentAddressPrefix (the NSG allow) and be peered
findings.why: A pool doesn't allow networks. After c4032df the real requirement is that the agents' range is in the 1433 allow rule (agentAddressPrefix, network.bicep) and that their network is peered to or inside the VNet. The pool comment at lines 21-24 doesn't mention the NSG range either. An agent outside agentAddressPrefix fails the migrations step. That fails closed, but the template sends the operator in the wrong direction. Code-quality rule: a comment explains the why, and it must be true.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: no secrets / config by environment
findings.what: agentAddressPrefix is a committed placeholder (10.30.0.0/24, the same in all 3 envs). The comment says 'not committed', but the pipeline has no override, so a commit is the only way to set it
findings.why: sqlAdminGroupObjectId has a placeholder plus a variable-group override (--parameters sqlAdminGroupObjectId=$(sqlAdminGroupObjectId)). agentAddressPrefix has no such path, so 'the real address range ... is not committed. Set it before the first deployment' can only be done by committing it. An address range isn't a secret, so committing it is fine. But the comment and the mechanism contradict each other, and David will be asked which one is intended. The same text appears in test.bicepparam and prod.bicepparam, line 10.

findings.rule_id: F5 AC2 (QA O1: approve prod after reading its what-if)
findings.what: WhatIf is a separate job but in the same stage (Deploy_<env>) as the policies-<env> deployment job, so the prod approval is still asked before the what-if runs. QA defect not resolved.
findings.why: Azure DevOps evaluates checks on protected resources per stage. The Approvals and checks docs say that before a stage can begin, all checks on all resources used in that stage must pass. The tester's own O1 (docs/qa/build-F5.md, observation O1) says the same and names the fix: a what-if-only stage before the prod deployment stage. c2af74d moved the what-if into its own job (lines 22-43) inside the stage that consumes environment policies-${{ parameters.environmentName }} (line 56). Deploy_prod therefore pauses for the policies-prod approval before WhatIf starts, which is the defect David ruled fix-now in gate.qa@925fe90. The comment at lines 19-21 ('it runs before any approval is asked for') is false under that model. Certainty: this rests on the documented stage-level check evaluation. I can't verify it against a live Azure DevOps, and nothing in the repo or receipts shows job-level evaluation. findings.what: design.md blames the JSON naming policy for ?REFERENCE=x giving the key 'reference'. The serializer never camel-cases error keys, and the app's helper turns COLOUR into cOLOUR.
findings.why: Lines 64-65 say: 'That is the JSON naming policy applied to the key.' The repo contradicts this in four places. (1) Program.cs:50-56 sets no DictionaryKeyPolicy, and the Web defaults camel-case property names only, not dictionary keys. (2) The comment at PoliciesController.cs:93 says 'ValidationProblem() does not camel-case keys, so the wire name is spelled out'. (3) docs/qa/build-F4.md:269-273 records, measured over HTTP, that the key 'Amount' came back unchanged. (4) The only key rewrite is ValidationProblems.CamelCase (ValidationProblems.cs:25-26), which lower-cases only the first letter of each dotted segment. So an unknown '?COLOUR=x' comes back as 'cOLOUR', not camelCase. 'reference' most likely appears because ModelState matches keys case-insensitively and merges 'REFERENCE' with the entry for the bound route parameter 'reference'. No test pins this (no REFERENCE in tests/). The F2 QA note (docs/qa/build-F2.md:214-217) put the JSON-policy cause forward only as a guess ('That looks like…'), and design.md now states it as fact under 'Two details that surprise people'. An assessor who tries another upper-case key will see the doc is wrong, and David cannot defend the stated cause. Fix direction: state what the repo proves and nothing more (for example, say the key is reported as bound or as sent, with the first letter lower-cased), or remove the explanation.

findings.what: 'Every problem' is said to carry type /problems/{rule-id}, ruleId and traceId. 400, 413, 429, 500 and the concurrency 409 have no ruleId, and their type is not a rule id.
findings.why: The table at line 55 already says a 400 has no ruleId, so the doc contradicts itself. UnexpectedExceptionHandler.cs:36 gives a 500 the type rfc9110#section-15.6.1 with no ruleId. The concurrency 409 is /problems/concurrency with no ruleId (UnexpectedExceptionHandler.cs:49), and a 429 is /problems/rate-limited (Program.cs:157). The requirements line (requirements.md:121) covers only 'every rule violation'. Narrow the sentence to rule violations (404, 409, 422).

findings.what: 'Only merged code reaches them' overclaims. The trigger limits CI runs only, so a manual run of any branch reaches the self-hosted pools unless a branch control check exists. None is documented.
findings.why: azure-pipelines.yml:5-9 sets only the CI trigger and pr: none. Azure DevOps lets anyone with queue rights run a pipeline manually against any branch, and that branch's YAML then runs on policies-<env>-vnet with the service connections. Nothing in the repo or the one-time setup list adds a branch control check that limits the environment or connections to main. The sentence presents a control that is not there. Either say a branch control check (main only) is part of the one-time setup, or soften the claim.

findings.what: Notes for David leak into the assessor docs. 'A decision the author should confirm' reads as unfinished work, and infrastructure/README.md:159 cites internal finding ids (F5 A2.3 R1).
findings.why: The acceptance (DAG F6) wants reference material for an assessor. design.md:210 asks the author to confirm decisions, which tells the reader they are not yet settled. infrastructure/README.md:154-159 names loop finding ids an outsider cannot resolve and says 'which the author would have to explain'. Either record David's ruling on each behaviour, or phrase them as stated behaviours with their reasons, and describe the checker gaps without the internal ids.

findings.what: Security scope and Known limits never say the deployed API is internet-facing with no edge WAF or Front Door, and that anyone with a guessable reference can read personal data.
findings.why: The skill's P2 row covers per-instance limits and no edge WAF when the README doesn't state it. The app has no ipSecurityRestrictions and no auth. GET returns names, dates of birth and addresses, and POST claims can zero a refund. The docs say only that the reference is the only key.

findings.what: design.md says the client IP is read from X-Forwarded-For when the proxy is in the private ranges, with no caveat that this is untested on App Service Linux.
findings.why: The untested caveat is only in infrastructure/README.md. I believe the App Service Linux front end shows a non-RFC1918 address and the platform may set ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED, but I did not verify either. If so, the per-IP limit and Request.IsHttps could misbehave; the main risk is all clients sharing one partition.

findings.what: The ?REFERENCE bullet now gives a false 'so', and its 'would be rEFERENCE' prediction contradicts the observation the same paragraph cites.
findings.why: Line 72 says 'A key the client sent keeps the rest of its casing, so an unknown query key that differs from a route parameter only in case (?REFERENCE=x) is a 400'. Casing does not cause the 400. RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:13-17 treats only Query-bound parameters as known, and the route-bound reference never is. Lower-case ?reference=X gives the same 400 (RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:84-95). The general rule 'keeps the rest of its casing' is contradicted by the only evidence for an upper-case key, docs/qa/build-F2.md:214-217, saw 'reference'. The 'rEFERENCE' prediction at :74 reads ValidationProblems.cs:25-26 alone. It skips the step where the filter's AddModelError (:25) writes the key into ModelState, whose key handling the repo neither documents nor tests. David cannot defend either sentence (CLAUDE.md: every line explainable). This is the third round on this bullet (A2 R1, I1, I2). Fix direction, per I1 and inv-003 rec 3: keep what is proven. Body and model error keys get the first letter of each segment lower-cased (ValidationProblems.cs:25-26). Any unknown query key is a 400, including one that differs only in case from a route parameter (filter :13-17; pinned for lower case only). The ?REFERENCE key was seen once by hand as 'reference' and is not pinned. Drop the 'so' and the rEFERENCE prediction.

findings.what: 'never a stack trace in the body' widens requirements.md:125, which says 'never a stack trace outside Development'. The only 500 test runs outside Development.
findings.why: UnhandledExceptionTests.cs:9 describes its case as 'outside Development'. requirements.md:125 limits the guarantee to outside Development, and no test exercises a 500 in Development. This is the same class as A2 R2/I3: a requirement sentence widened past its scope. Narrow it to 'outside Development', or cite a Development test.

findings.what: Three 'all/except' sentences are wider than the code: all routes on PoliciesController (:27), rules in the domain except SELL-1 (:147), tester/builder commits carry TDD (:139).
findings.why: (1) Program.cs:121-127 maps /openapi, /scalar and /health/* outside the controller, so 'All routes are on PoliciesController' holds only for the policy routes. The claim table's source ('the only controller') proves the narrower sentence. (2) GET-1 is also produced in the service, not the domain (PolicyService.cs:57-60, 139-143). (3) .githooks/commit-msg:36-38 exempts docs( subjects from TDD, as design.md:126 itself says, and the hook only runs on feature/* and bug/* branches (:6-9). Each is small. inv-003 rec 1 gives only/every/all/except sentences the closest check, and these three were not narrowed.

findings.what: Claim-table line refs are wrong across whole files: appservice.bicep :128-174 (77 lines), sql.bicep :189-253 (92), stage-template.yml :155-238 (159), ProblemCatalog.cs :50-76 (40).
findings.why: The table's 'limits' entry says these line numbers 'are correct at daa4876'. They are not. The offsets are consistent: appservice +102 (httpsOnly is :37, not :139), sql +178 (admin block :20-27, not :198-205), monitoring.bicep cites :134 but the file has 28 lines (the description is at :26), and stage-template is +80 except :58. So the content was read, but from a concatenated listing, and attributed to the wrong lines. Policy.cs refs drift too: Payment!.Method is :167, not :164-165; RENEW-3b is :154, not :150; the detail texts are :135/:148/:172, not :128-132/:146/:161. launchSettings applicationUrl is :19, not :22. The source for README:68, 'ProblemCatalog.cs:69-74 (the same 12 ids map to 422)', describes a mapping that does not exist: StatusFor maps ViolationKind (:30-35), and the 422/409 split comes from Policy.cs Violation versus Conflict. Every sentence I opened holds against the real lines, so the docs are not wrong. But someone checking the trace (inv-003 rec 1) cannot follow these refs, and the table vouches for its own accuracy without grounds.

findings.what: 'which aren't auto-created from YAML' (setup step 5) is stated as fact, but its only source is X. No repo file proves it, and it is a claim about Azure DevOps behaviour.
findings.why: inv-003 rec 1 (accepted): anything that can't be traced is removed or marked as untested. claims.json lists this sentence under limits[2] as not provable and anchors it only to docs/readme-checklist.md:22, which states the obligation, not the fact. I can't check this here, but as I recall Microsoft's documentation says a YAML deployment job that names a missing environment can create it. Following step 5 still works either way; only the stated reason is at risk. Fix direction: say only that the four environments must be created with the prod approval, or mark the clause as unverified. This is spec wording, so David may need to decide.

findings.what: :74 says task inputs, service connections and environments 'are not checked'. But :77-79 and :83 say the checker asserts AzureCLI@2 inputs, the azureSubscription form and the env name.
findings.why: check-pipeline.py:83-86 asserts the four AzureCLI@2 inputs on the deploying stage. :205-208 asserts every azureSubscription is a template parameter. :112 asserts 'environment: policies-${{ parameters.environmentName }}'. So the sentence's cited source (docs/readme-checklist.md:24) carries the obligation to use this wording, and the code contradicts two parts of it. The paragraph at :77-79 softens this ('does not validate those values against Azure DevOps'), so a careful reader gets there, but :74 still reads as false on its own. Fix direction: make the sentence say what is not checked, such as 'against Azure DevOps', or have David rule on the verbatim spec text.

findings.what: 'A term with a claim (COULD-2) ... gets no Refund record' reads as per-term. The code applies COULD-2 to every paid term of a policy that has any claim.
findings.why: Policy.cs:257 passes the policy-level HasClaims to RefundCalculator.ForTerm for every term. RefundCalculator.cs:30-32 then returns (COULD-2, 0) for any paid term, including a future renewal term. requirements.md:102 says 'No refund if the policy has a claim'. This sentence's own sources (RefundCalculator.cs:30 'hasClaims') prove the policy-wide rule, not the per-term one. The same quantifier-scope class as A3 R3. Fix direction: 'every paid term of a policy with a claim (COULD-2)'.

findings.what: README:66 'still lists every term with refundAmount 0.00' can read as every term being 0.00. requirements.md:108 qualifies it with ruleApplied COULD-2 or UNPAID-TERM.
findings.why: A3 raised this as a non-blocking note. It is still unchanged in the assessor-facing README, and the brief weights 'every' sentences. requirements.md:108 reads 'still lists every term, with refundAmount 0.00 and ruleApplied COULD-2 or UNPAID-TERM'. design.md:174 has the right scope ('Its calculation is still in the response'). Fix direction: 'still lists each such term, with refundAmount 0.00'.

findings.what: The 'Run it' steps go ci, build, preview, then 'The Overview', with no 'npm run trace'. On a fresh clone the build has no trace.json, so the explorer shows its data notice, not the Overview.
findings.why: §7 Run it (static build) and LRN-5 (what you should see). In U10, src/Uinsure.Policies.Web/.gitignore ignores public/. traceOnStart in vite.config.ts applies only to 'serve', and the 'build' script is plain 'vite build'. The pipeline's Web stage runs 'run trace' before 'run build'. As printed, step 4's expected screen is false. The fix is in the guide's own troubleshooting row, not in the steps.

findings.what: The printed reader commands target the capture ports. curl hits 4186/5096 right after the guide starts 4170/5080, and the Postman CLI line forces baseUrl=http://localhost:5096. Both fail as printed.
findings.why: David's P1 bar is a printed command that fails as printed. §2 step 2 starts the API on 5080 and the preview on 4170, and MAN-1 step 2 says to start the API on 5080. Then §2 step 3 (curl 4186, 5096) and MAN-2 (line 246, --env-var baseUrl=...5096) hit ports nothing is listening on. The receipts are real (activity.jsonl), but they belong in the output block, not in the command the reader runs.

findings.what: 'npx playwright show-report' and 'a trace opens in the trace viewer' don't hold: playwright.config.ts sets no html reporter (the default is list) and no use.trace. No report or trace is ever written.
findings.why: MAN-5 requires opening the HTML report and the trace viewer. In U10, src/Uinsure.Policies.Web/playwright.config.ts has no 'reporter' and no 'trace', so 'npm run e2e' writes no playwright-report folder. show-report then finds no report, and the claim about the trace viewer is false. This was marked 'not run', but the disclosure covers the missing output, not a command that can't work.

findings.what: The npx playwright and npx vitest lines run from the repo root, which has no package.json, so npx can't reach the pinned @playwright/test 1.62.0 or vitest 5.0.5.
findings.why: Static evidence; these commands weren't run. The --config src/Uinsure.Policies.Web/... paths mean the root is the working directory. The U10 root has no package.json, so npx would offer to download an unpinned playwright or vitest. The specs resolve @playwright/test through the web project's tsconfig paths, and a second Playwright copy refuses to run the tests. 'npx playwright install chromium' (line 260) may also install browsers for the wrong version. The fix is to run them from src/Uinsure.Policies.Web or through npm --prefix ... exec.

findings.what: The One rule step 2 says '(marker 2)', but the ex-rule figure has only marker 1. The marker text is hand-typed in build.mjs, not taken from the manifest.
findings.why: LRN-6 says markers are measured, never placed by hand. Hand-typed marker references drift from the measured set in the same way.

'exec -- playwright install chromium' and the troubleshooting row are fine, because they take no path. findings.what: The activity chunk mapping drops `attempt`, so every Attempt cell on the activity page shows a dash, and the page says a dash means the log has no value. The log has one.
findings.why: Every activity.jsonl line carries attempt (e.g. docs/trace/ui/U0b/activity.jsonl:1, and the complete fixture's lines 1-5 hold attempt 1). The signed-off contract reads trace/<plan>/<node>/activity.json[].attempt (docs/ui/derived/U0b/activity/screen.json:17,26). Activity.tsx:46 renders `row.record.attempt ?? GAP`, and Activity.tsx:107 tells the reader 'A dash means the log holds none for that column'. Showing an absence the trail contradicts is a claim that isn't in the trail (ui-requirements HONEST-1; principle 'show the receipt, not the claim'). The fix belongs in the compiler (carry attempt into the chunk), not in the screen.

findings.what: The activity row read-back checks Line, Agent, Tool, command, Commit and TDD but skips Attempt. The compiler's chunk test maps only agent/tool/file/command. Neither sees R1.
findings.why: Success tests must read the resource back in full through the shared assertion (reviewer check 3; requirements-trace 'Stub-proof success rows'). A partial read-back let a missing column pass 64/64 at loop.jsonl:71. tests/web/unit/compiler/data-1.test.ts:103 likewise omits attempt (and ts) from the chunk shape. No HONEST-1-tagged test asserts the activity values against the fixture trail. A red test should assert Attempt = 1 on rows 1-5 of the complete fixture, plus a chunk-shape assertion that includes attempt.

findings.what: Only the commit subject goes through the denylist scan. Emitted trailer values (Rule, Agent, Plan, Node, TDD, Fixes-Finding) and compiledAt.ref reach trace.json unscanned.
findings.why: DATA-5: 'The compiler fails the build if its output matches the privacy denylist'. The data-5 unit test header claims the scan covers 'every value it emits'. That is not so: index.ts:112-124 emits commits[].agent/plan/node/rule/tdd/fixesFinding from commit bodies, and :206 emits ref, with no scan(). Nothing else guards these values: .githooks/pre-commit scans staged files only, and commit-msg checks the Rule trailer only for being non-empty, so its free text is unguarded. The exposure is narrow (Agent, TDD and Fixes-Finding are pattern-checked by commit-msg), but the rule's guarantee isn't met and no test plants a denylisted trailer. Fix direction: scan the serialised output, or every emitted git-derived value, and add a red test with a denylisted Rule trailer.

findings.what: trailersOf uses Object.fromEntries, so a repeated trailer key keeps only its last value. Commits with several Fixes-Finding lines lose all but the last in trace.json.
findings.why: This trail repeats Fixes-Finding lines: 380ef5f has A1/I1 and A1/I2, and 99e9d93 has A2/I1, A2/I3 and A2/I4 (packet/trailers.txt). fixesFinding() at index.ts expects a comma list, but the trail writes one line per finding, so the compiled commits[].fixesFinding misstates the trail. No U0b screen reads it yet, but LOOP-2 (the retry ladder) will, and no test covers repeated trailers. That is why this is P2 and not P1.

findings.what: The compiler fills events, verdicts and rules[].status/feature/red/green with parsing logic that no U0b test drives and no U0b screen reads.
findings.why: The loop.jsonl event parse (:154-163), the verdict envelope and round parse (:164-179) and the rule status derivation (:189-200) have no red test in tests/web/unit/compiler (the DATA-1 tests check only the rule ids and the commit fields). The trace-data schema needs the lists to exist, but filling them with untested logic is code not driven by a red commit (web-testing: green follows red), and it is speculative for this node (code-quality slop list). Either test it here or emit empty lists until U1/U3 drive it.

findings.what: The overview and node page say a node has 'no trail' when completeness is null. They ignore the compiler's trail flag, which TraceNode doesn't declare.
findings.why: The compiler emits nodes[*].trail (src/web/compiler/index.ts:228, pinned by data-4.test.ts). findings.what: TraceRule.status is typed string, but the compiler emits null for a rule with no matrix row.
findings.why: index.ts sets status to cells === null ? null : …, and data-1.test.ts asserts null. The loader type claims a string is always there. The screens happen to handle null as 'not built', but the type hides the case from the compiler's checks.

findings.what: The matrix links any non-empty PR cell as /pull/<text>, while the rule page links only a cell that matches ^#(\d+)$.
findings.why: NAV-3 and the react-web rule say links out are built from IDs in trace.json, never from free text. Every real PR cell today is '#<n>', so nothing is wrong on screen. But the two screens parse the same cell two ways, and a cell like 'pending' would become a GitHub link on the matrix.

findings.what: A P0 finding is passed to VerdictCard as P2 (`f.severity === 'P1' ? 'P1' : 'P2'`), so the page's own findings region says P0 while its verdict card says P2.
findings.why: LOOP-3 says each verdict is rendered from its JSON. The verdict schema allows P0 (rule broken or exploitable), and this code would show it as the least severe level. Ladder.tsx:85 has the same coercion, so the loop and node pages show it too. The kit's VerdictCard takes only 'P1' | 'P2' (VerdictCard.tsx:14). react-web says a missing kit variant is reported as a kit change, never worked around in the screen, and HONEST-1 can't be waived. No fixture verdict holds a P0 and no test asserts severity, so the suite can't see this.

findings.what: Every node's loop page says 'each event recorded by the orchestrator', but 37 events in 7 real loop logs have source 'reconciled', and the compiled `source` field is ignored.
findings.why: DATA-2 keeps each item's provenance, and HONEST-1 forbids a name the trail doesn't hold. The reference sentence was true for the design fixture's F3. The screen turned it into a fixed claim for every node, including build/F1 (lines 56-72), F0b, U0b, U1, U3 (line 29) and W1, whose reconciled lines were added afterwards.

findings.what: resultOf maps a gate event with no recorded ok to 'waived', which the kit words as 'Waived' (the gate did not run). The log records no waiver, and the code's own comment says 'did not decide'.
findings.why: LOOP-1 shows ok as the line records it. The kit's GateRow defines waived as 'the gate was waived, so it did not run' (GateRow.tsx:11), which is a claim the log line doesn't make. No real gate line lacks ok today, so nothing shows it yet.

findings.what: A finding whose testable is null is passed to FindingCard as testable=false, so the card is headed 'Untestable' while the line above it says 'testable: not recorded'.
findings.why: LOOP-4 shows 'testable or not' as recorded. Turning null into false invents an untestable verdict (HONEST-1), and the page then contradicts itself. The compiler keeps testable null when the round doesn't hold a boolean (compiler/index.ts).

findings.what: splitRootCause keeps only the text after the first Symptom, Cause or Fix direction marker. It drops any preamble and any repeated marker's segment, yet the page labels the rest recorded.
findings.why: LOOP-4 shows each finding's symptom, cause and fix direction, and DATA-2 'recorded' means the agent's judgement stored verbatim. When any marker is present, text[0..marks[0].index] is never kept, and `if (name in found) return` (:238) also drops the segment after a repeated marker. Real trails lose text today. U3's own A2 I1 to I5 open with 'Layer: the kit ... It is recorded as api because the schema's layer enum has no ui layer', so the finding page shows 'layer api' without the investigator's correction. build/F1 A1 loses 'Source Rn.', build/F1 D1 loses 'New, from the ... ruling.', and F0b A1 loses 'Layer note: ...'. Separately, 'Cause (kit):' doesn't match, so the cause text sits under Symptom while Cause shows the no-marker gap. The fixture root_causes all start with 'Symptom:', so no test can see this. The finding page has no in-app raw text to fall back on. This is the same triage case as A2/I2: real trails show it, so it blocks. Route: a red test first, on a fixture round whose root_cause has a preamble and a repeated marker, then the compiler fix.

findings.what: severityOf turns a missing or unknown severity into P2 on the verdict card. The page's findings region shows the same value as recorded, in the fail tone, so the two disagree.
findings.why: The A2/I1 fix direction (findings/A2.md) says a severity outside P0 to P2 'should show as recorded, never be mapped to another level', and the function's own comment admits the fallback. Verdict.tsx:585 tones anything but P2 as fail and shows the text as written, so one page gives two answers. The verdict schema allows only P0, P1 and P2, so no hook-checked file reaches this. It doesn't block.

findings.what: The accepted U7 carries are missing from ui.dag.yaml: A2/I3 (an ok-less gate drawn Waived), A2/I4 (a null testable drawn Untestable), the pause-1 DATA-2 labels on loop events, and t6's kit notes.
findings.why: The defects behind these deferrals are still in the code at HEAD: Ladder.tsx:19 maps ok null to waived, and Finding.tsx:89 passes testable null as false. Loop events and ladder verdicts carry no ProvenanceLabel, although DATA-2 says the label is shown 'wherever the item appears'. Two kit workarounds also sit in the screen: a trailing space in the FindingCard id at Finding.tsx:83, and the '(then …)' subject in fixOf. Each was made non-blocking only on the promise of a U7 line (loop.jsonl:10, :15 and :36, inv-007 recommendation 3, all 'added when U3 integrates after U2'). 6f29830 integrated U2, and U7's acceptance list (ui.dag.yaml:420-444) holds none of them. The lines must exist before merge, or the deferrals are lost. This is a plan edit, recorded against the code that carries the defect.

findings.what: ad2105d and f5f98c8 are fix(...) commits with no Fixes-Finding trailer. They repair the U2 merge, not a finding.
findings.why: requirements-trace says a fix(…) commit carries Fixes-Finding. Both are merge repairs proven by the failing e2e at 6f29830 (loop.jsonl:57), not finding fixes. They should use a non-fix type, or name what they fix, so the LOOP-2 ladder and the trace stay truthful about which commits fix findings.

findings.what: splitRootCause treats a marker quoted in prose ('Symptom:', "Cause:") as a split point: U3's own A3 I1 and I2 show cause text under Symptom and Fix direction, and the quoted words are lost.
findings.why: The marker pattern /(Symptom|Cause|Fix direction)(\s*\([^)]*\))?:/g has no anchor, so it matches every occurrence anywhere in the text, including quoted mentions. With the new join-in-order behaviour, each quoted mention moves the text that follows it into the field it names. The real trail shows it on this node's own round, docs/trace/ui/U3/findings/A3.md:13, the only round whose root_cause quotes a marker. In I1, the Cause field stops at "long-content.html:33 says 'Where a sentence comes before the \"". The rest of the cause (the long-content quote, the retry-ladder README critique, the p0-reconciled note) is appended to Symptom through the quoted "Symptom:" and 'Symptom:'. In I2, the quoted 'Fix direction:' makes the Fix direction field open with "'. Real rounds also write qualified forms. docs/trace/ui/U3/findings/A2.md:14 has '". The quoted 'Symptom (security S1, P2, verdict PASS):' sends the middle of the cause ("An unmatched qualified marker is not a split point ... HONEST-1 forbids naming a gap ('no") to Symptom, and the quoted 'Cause:' and "Cause:" words disappear from the text. That is R1's symptom from A3: cause text under the Symptom label, on a real trail, on a page that labels the text 'recorded' (DATA-2). The function's own doc comment (:232) says 'Every character lands in a field', which is false here. The tests can't see it. Every new fixture text uses markers only at sentence starts, and expectEveryWord's MARKER_NAME (loop-4.test.ts:170) strips every marker name wherever it appears, so a dropped quoted marker word passes. The A3/I1 fix direction asked that every character of the recorded root_cause end up in some field. Route: first a red test on a fixture root_cause that quotes a marker inside a sentence (for example "Cause: it matches only 'Symptom:' and 'Cause:'. Fix direction: F1."), then the compiler fix. This is narrower than A3's R1 but the same defect on the node's own trail, so it blocks by the same bar.

findings.what: A path result opens blobUrl(sha, entry.href), and entry.href is '#/files/<encoded path>', so the link is REPO/blob/<sha>/#/files/docs%2F..., which never opens the file.
findings.why: NAV-4: 'Jump to any ... file path from one input'. searchIndex (src/web/app/data/trace.ts:361) gives a path entry the href `#/files/${seg(path)}`. No app route answers that href, and SiteSearch passes it to blobUrl(sha, path) (repo.ts:10) as the file path. Choosing any path match therefore goes to the GitHub repo root at the snapshot SHA with a junk fragment, not to the file. The path jump half of NAV-4 doesn't work.

findings.what: lanesOf drops every activity line whose agent isn't in the kit's AgentName list, so web-tester, web-builder and kit-builder lines vanish from the ui plan's lanes with no notice.
findings.why: AGENT-2 asks for activity.jsonl as per-agent lanes that show the agents working in sequence. DATA-8 says lines are 'never silently dropped', and HONEST-1 applies too. agentOf (shell/agents.ts) returns null for any name outside main/tester/builder/reviewer/security/investigator/git/david, and `if (agent === null) continue;` skips that line. In docs/trace/ui/U4/activity.jsonl most of the 468 lines are web-tester, web-builder or kit-builder, so this node's own activity page would show only main and git. The FilterBar above still counts every record in matchCount/totalCount, so the lane view and the count disagree. The agents fixture uses only build-plan names, so no test catches this. Needs a fixture line with a ui-plan agent, and either a kit AgentName change or a labelled lane for unknown agents.

findings.what: The path search tests check only that a path option is offered. No unit or e2e test checks where a path result goes, so R1 passed every gate.
findings.why: Anti-oracle: the rule, node and SHA tests each check the URL the choice opens, and the path test checks nothing after the offer. nav-4.test.ts 'part of a path finds the path' checks [kind, label] only and leaves out href. A canned href passes both.

findings.what: The test title says 'Enter on it opens the node page', but the test presses ArrowDown and then clicks the option. It never presses Enter, so keyboard selection is unproven.
findings.why: A test asserts the behaviour its title claims (web-testing rule tag; anti-oracle). Keyboard activation of the combobox result is not exercised anywhere in the U4 suite.

findings.what: The rule-page command `git log --reverse <red>^..<green>` says 'Expect red first ... green last', which doesn't hold when a merge lands between red and green.
findings.why: VERIFY-1: the command must re-check the claim without the UI. U4 itself merged origin/ui (eddb436) between its red and green commits. With a merge, red^..green includes the merged branch's commits, and `--reverse` can list older merged commits before red. The printed expectation is then false even though the trail is fine. Related: on the about page (About.tsx:67), the 'Expect red, stub, green or refactor' text leaves out scaffold, a valid TDD trailer.

findings.what: The 'ruling' kind is mapped in KINDS and KIND_WORDS, but the compiler never emits it and no loop event or fixture holds one. The branch is dead, and HITL-1's rulings are silently absent.
findings.why: Code-quality slop list: dead branch. HITL-1 lists rulings among the decisions. The node acceptance narrows the list to pause, steer, sign-off and merge, so this doesn't block. But the page's question ('What did David decide across the nodes') reads as complete while rulings are recorded only in detail text (for example loop.jsonl:38). Either drop the dead kind, or say on the page that rulings aren't extracted.

verdicts.head: acf9a9bffde63f29a558d12fd36c129b2e19d5cc

findings.what: A path result's GitHub link is built from the hash route, not the path: blobUrl(sha, entry.href) gives .../blob/<sha>/#/files/<enc>.
findings.why: W2 says links are built from IDs in trace.json. The host is fixed to the repo, so nothing can be injected. But the link opens the commit root, not the file, and nav-4 only checks the option exists, not its href. Use entry.label.

findings.what: External evidence links (GitHub blob URLs from DecisionRow.tsx:55) have no rel="noreferrer". ShaLink's GitHub link has the same gap.
findings.why: W2 asks for rel="noreferrer" on external links. The links open in the same tab, so there is no opener risk. The cost is a Referer leak to GitHub. Hygiene only.

findings.what: The tour's Walkthrough and Commit stops link to the first node that has a walkthrough, not to the node of the rule the Rule stop opens, though the copy says 'the commits of its node'.
findings.why: NAV-5 asks for a path through one rule end to end. rule.matrix.node and plan are in TraceRule, so stops 3 to 5 could follow the same rule. On the real trail the Rule stop opens the first built rule and the Walkthrough stop opens an unrelated node. The signed-off reference also links unrelated pages (GET-1 with F3), so this doesn't block the node.

findings.what: Only the hrefs of the Overview and Requirements matrix stops are pinned. The Rule, Walkthrough and Commit stop targets have no test, so R1's mismatch goes unseen.
findings.why: web-testing: a behaviour test proves the node's flows. The computed hrefs of stops 3 to 5 are the only data-driven part of the tour, and nothing tests them.

findings.what: The page draws 'commits per agent' as a gap ('this page's data holds ... not commits'), but trace.json's commits[] carries each commit's Agent trailer, so the figure could be computed.
findings.why: The STATS-1 row names commits per agent, attempts per node and elapsed time. The build follows the signed-off G4 stats screen, which draws both as gaps, and that screen is the contract. Whether the gap stands is David's call at pause 2. It isn't U5's to change.

findings.what: The reference's 'Sort the table by its first column' action (sortable Node column, aria-sort) isn't built. The DataTable gets no sortable column and no sort or onSortChange.
findings.why: docs/ui/derived/U5/stats/screen.json lists the sort as an action, and populated.html draws the header as a sort button with aria-sort. The structural parity checks don't look at it.

findings.what: DAG task t1 names a compiler unit test for the harness file. No AGENT-3 unit test exists, as the tester noted in gate.red.
findings.why: ui.dag.yaml U5 t1: 'unit tests (compiler: context snapshots, the harness file, delivery stats)'. The pass-through may be covered by the earlier DATA-7 tests, but the node's own rule has no compiler-level test.

findings.what: Dead test support: rowOf, mainText, the rowTexts re-export and route.plan aren't used by any U5 spec.
findings.why: This is code-quality slop: unused members. The same kind of finding already sits in U7 for U0b's support file (W1 review A4 R1).

findings.what: A context snapshot's file path and filename slug go into trace.json sessions[] without being scanned against the denylist.
findings.why: W5/W6 and DATA-5: the compiler says a git path only after scanning it, as it does for plan files at lines 206-207. The body is scanned through read(), but the filename is not. The slug appears on the Sessions page. Hygiene only: /save-context writes the filenames and the real ones are clean.

findings.what: No test shows that a denylist hit inside a docs/context snapshot (front matter or body) fails the compile with no trace.json written.
findings.why: W5 and DATA-5 on the new CTX-1 boundary. The behaviour holds through read() (line 291), but data-5.test.ts has no docs/context case, so a later change to the read path could drop the scan unnoticed.

findings.what: Renew, QuoteCancel and RecordClaim still render t2 stub content at HEAD: another policy's reference, dates and amounts, and Renew/Cancel/Record buttons with no handler.
findings.why: docs/ui/derived/W1/derived.json marks these regions as built by W1: wb-renew's WB-3 problems and BUSY-1 renew-busy, wb-cancel's BUSY-1 actions and WB-3 problems, wb-claim's WB-3 problems and BUSY-1 record-claim. The routes are live and linked from the policy view ('Quote a cancellation', 'Record a claim'). For any :reference they show F4-MVFJSC6LXX, a 422 for 2027-09-18..2027-10-18, 'Cancel on 2026-12-02' and amount 401.16. None of that comes from the API's answer, which breaks HONEST-1 (MUST, can't be waived) and react-web ('every value comes from trace.json, the API's answer or the kit's labelled placeholder… never a default'). The buttons are never busy or disabled, so BUSY-1 isn't met on them. The 'Stub: … The client replaces it' comments (QuoteCancel.tsx:5, RecordClaim.tsx:5, Renew.tsx:6) are leftovers after green. No e2e spec or parity Screen covers these three screens: parity.ts types screen as wb-home|wb-sell|wb-policy only. Either build and test these regions, or render them as NotBuiltRegion and have David correct the derived reference or plan scope (t6 names only home, sell and policy).

findings.what: The shell works around the kit's RuleChip default href with a global MutationObserver that rewrites React-owned <a href='/rules/…'> to '#/rules/…' in the live DOM.
findings.why: react-web: 'A missing or wrong component is a kit change: stop and report it, never patch it in the screen.' The file's own comment says 'A kit change (a link prefix) would make this unnecessary.' The patch is also unsound. It watches only childList, but React updates an existing anchor's href through an attribute mutation, which isn't observed. If the summary re-renders with a different violation on a reused <a> (a second 422), the chip goes back to '/rules/<id>', a non-hash path, and WB-3's 'rule chip that links to RULE-1' breaks. The WB-3 e2e checks only the first render. It also rewrites explorer links app-wide. This should go to David as a kit change (a RuleChip link base, or hrefs passed through ErrorSummary, ProblemBanner and SendAnywayToggle).

findings.what: WB-2's refunds, claims and cancellation are tested only as empty or null. No test at either layer shows a policy with a refund, a claim or a cancellation rendered from the API.
findings.why: WB-2's interpretation lists 'payments, refunds, claims'. The live API already has E3 (cancel) and E5 (claims), so a test can cancel a sold policy (a refund greater than 0, cancellation set) or record a claim, then read the view against the API's GET. PolicyView.tsx:156-189 duck-types refund {reference,type,amount,paymentReference}, claim {reference,claimDate,description} and cancellation {cancellationDate,ruleApplied,totalRefund} from unknown. Nothing proves those rows or the timeline claim and cancellation rungs. A view that always rendered 'no refunds' or 'no claims' would pass every WB-2 test, so those success rows aren't stub-proof. The unit tests (wb-2.test.ts) also assert only the empty lists.

findings.what: ask() parses response.json() inside the fetch try, so an HTTP answer with a non-JSON body is reported as 'unreachable' ('The API did not answer') and its status is dropped.
findings.why: WB-3 says to render the answer the API gave. When a request reached the API, or the proxy answered with a status, the UI shouldn't say no request completed. Separate the network failure from a body that can't be read, and keep the status.

findings.what: NoPolicy says 'the policy was not found' for any problem status, including a 400 for a route reference that fails the pattern.
findings.why: The API answers 400 for a route reference that fails ^[A-Z0-9-]{3,20}$ (architecture: strict input), and 404 only under GET-1. Calling a 400 'not found' is a claim the API didn't make (HONEST-1). Word it from the problem's status or title.

findings.what: Policy.refunds, claims and cancellation are typed unknown, although the API contract fixes their shapes, so PolicyView probes string keys at runtime.
findings.why: api.md gives the shapes of refunds[], claims (ClaimResponse) and cancellation. Typed interfaces would let tsc catch a misnamed field (claimDate, totalRefund) and remove the duck-typing helpers. That reads better for David to explain line by line (code-quality).

findings.what: A 2xx answer whose body isn't JSON returns kind 'ok' with value undefined cast to Policy. sellPolicy and getPolicy then throw on answer.value.reference, and the Sell button stays busy.
findings.why: The I4 fix catches the parse error but makes the 'ok' branch lie about its type. remember() dereferences .reference (lines 288 and 294), so the promise rejects. SellPolicy.send never resets inFlight, and PolicyView stays on 'waiting for the API'. BUSY-1 says 'When the process ends, the control re-enables and the result or problem appears.' WB-3 renders the answer the API gave. The configured proxy makes this unlikely, but the type should not claim a Policy it doesn't hold.

findings.what: Only the error summary's and the problem banner's chip hrefs are asserted. The send-anyway list's chips and the timeline's ruleApplied chip get ruleHref, but no test checks their href.
findings.why: RuleLinks.ts used to rewrite every chip in the document. Now that it's gone, each composite has to receive ruleHref (gate.green 00:17:23Z lists SendAnywayToggle and TermTimeline). If SendAnywayToggle (SellPolicy.tsx:393) or TermTimeline (PolicyView.tsx:86) lost the prop, those chips would fall back to '/rules/<id>', which isn't a route in the hash app, and every W1 test would still pass. WB-3: 'each violation as a rule chip that links to RULE-1 for that rule'.

findings.what: The rule-page link '#/rules/' + ruleId is written four times: ProblemView.tsx:4, PolicyView.tsx:86 and SellPolicy.tsx:251 and :393.
findings.why: code-quality, rule of three: extract on the third occurrence when the copies change for the same reason. All four change if RULE-1's route changes. ProblemView already has a ruleHref const that it doesn't export.

findings.what: .s-wb-list isn't used by any file under src/web/app since Renew, QuoteCancel and RecordClaim were deleted.
findings.why: code-quality slop list: dead code. 99b3e57 removed the three unbuilt screens (inv-006 recommendation 1), and their layout class stayed behind.

findings.what: answerOf hard-codes 'The API answered 201' instead of the status received; the receipts also fall back to literal 200 (line 161) and 201 (line 190)
findings.why: HONEST-1: no number the data doesn't hold. react-web: every value comes from the API's answer. The status is in cancelling.status, but the header writes its own. The fallbacks can't be reached, but they are invented values.

findings.what: Header 'Policy status' comes from one GET on mount, so after a 201 cancel on the same screen it still shows the pre-cancel status (e.g. Active)
findings.why: WB-4 shows a successful cancel; HONEST-1: a status shown must be the one the API holds now. A re-read after the 201, or labelling the status as of load, would keep it honest.

findings.what: Local ruleHref = '#/rules/' + ruleId, unencoded, a new copy beside src/web/app/shell/ruleLinks.ts
findings.why: Same issue as U7's 'one shared helper builds every workbench rule link' (W1 review A3 R3). This adds another instance for that line to cover, rather than a new blocker. Rule of three: this is a third or later copy.

findings.what: The 'quote and cancellation agree (068)' unit test feeds two recorded answers through a pass-through client and compares them: it proves the fixture, not the code
findings.why: Anti-oracle: the client doesn't decide agreement, so this test can't fail for a code fault. The live e2e comparison tests do prove WB-4's 'agree', so coverage isn't lost.

findings.what: The refusals list now uses .s-wb-list, which U7 plans to delete as unused (W1 review A3 R4)
findings.why: U7's acceptance line no longer holds after W2. If it runs as written, it removes a style W2's screen uses. The U7 line needs revising, not the code.

findings.what: No test checks that the renew screen shows an accepted renewal. The only success test is a client unit test on a made-up 201, which a stub that only echoes would pass.
findings.why: WB-5 includes 'renew inside the window'. RenewPolicy.tsx handles the success path (the 'Renewed…' answer, and `shown = renewal.value` drawing the new term last on the timeline), but no e2e or screen test reaches it. The e2e comment scopes it out. tests/web/unit/client/wb-5.test.ts:78 only checks that renewPolicy hands back the body it was served. A page.route answer of 201, the same made-up body the unit test already uses, could drive the screen. Each rule row needs a success test that a stub can't pass (reviewer check 3).

findings.what: The default-method test sells with 'Card', which is also the screen's starting value and its fallback. A screen that never reads the term's method still passes.
findings.why: Anti-oracle rule: the value a test sets must differ from what a stub or the code's default would produce. Here the test value equals the screen's starting state and its fallback (RenewPolicy.tsx:24 and :68). It never proves that the payment-method default comes from the current term. Selling with DirectDebit would.

findings.what: The request log keeps no headers and rebuilds bodies by parsing and re-stringifying them, so the page can't show the exact exchange the signed-off wb-requests reference shows.
findings.why: WB-7 asks for 'the exact request and response of every action'. docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-requests/populated.html:33 shows 'Request headers (6)' and 'Response headers (4)' inside http-exchange. LoggedExchange has no headers, and RequestLogPage.tsx gives HttpExchange none. JSON.parse also loses the API's own number formatting (100.00 becomes 100). Parity passed because it compares data-comp structure only. No wb-7 test asserts headers, so the tests need a matching addition.

findings.what: termMethod falls back to 'Card' when the term's payment isn't found or isn't recognised. The form then shows a method the API never returned.
findings.why: react-web, 'Screens are composed': a value the data doesn't hold renders as an empty or 'not built' state, never as a default (HONEST-1). The code-quality slop list also counts invented behaviour.

findings.what: A request still waiting for its answer shows in the log table with status 0 (`entry.status ?? 0`). The API never returned that status.
findings.why: HONEST-1: no number may appear that isn't in the data. A pending or unanswered exchange should look pending or unanswered, as the drawer already does with outcome 'pending'.

findings.what: unique() builds policy references from Date.now(), in wb-5.spec.ts:10 and wb-7.spec.ts:11. The test data then depends on the time of the run.
findings.why: Anti-oracle rule: no random or time-of-day data, and each test passes its own literal reference. The e2e API starts on a fresh database (web-testing, 'Running'), so a literal reference per test would be unique enough.

findings.what: No test checks the components in wb-policy's actions region. The page draws three links where the signed-off reference has three kit Buttons plus the link list (PolicyView.tsx:405).
findings.why: docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-policy/populated.html:78-80 has data-comp 'button · primitive · primary' and two 'secondary' buttons in the actions region. react-web says a screen keeps each component's data-comp root, and web-testing's parity says the same. W1's parity now compares this region by place only and leaves its components to W3 (W1/support/parity.ts header). W3's wb-policy.spec checks only the region's data-req, so nothing catches the missing buttons. g4-defects.md has no ruling that lets them go, unlike the wb-requests filter-bar.

findings.what: 'Requests that touched this policy' matches paths by substring, so policy ABC also lists requests to /policies/ABC-2. No behaviour test covers what the region shows.
findings.why: entry.path.includes(`/policies/${reference}`) has no path-segment boundary. References are chosen by the seller (WB-1), so sharing a prefix is plausible, and the region would then show exchanges that never touched this policy (HONEST-1).
