findings.source: docs/trace/build/F6/verdicts/A3-reviewer.json R1, R2, R3, R4; docs/trace/build/F6/verdicts/A3-security.json (PASS, no findings) (round A3, head daa4876)
findings.cause: Reviewer R1, part 1 of 2. I split R1 in two on purpose; I2 covers the other half. There is no docs layer, so I use 'api' as in A2. SYMPTOM: docs/design.md:72-74 links the ?REFERENCE 400 to casing with 'so', then says 'By that code its key would be rEFERENCE'. The only observation, docs/qa/build-F2.md:214-217, saw 'reference'. CAUSE: the doc predicts the key from one file. The source of that reading is the A2 investigation itself. findings/A2.md:14, I1(c), says "On that code alone, 'REFERENCE' would become 'rEFERENCE'". I2 in the same file says "By the code, an unknown ?COLOUR=x would be keyed 'cOLOUR' (filter :25, then ValidationProblems.cs:26)". The builder copied that reasoning, and claims.json:518 cites 'ValidationProblems.cs:25-26 (code reading, not run)'. The reading skips a step the reviewer named. RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:25 calls ModelState.AddModelError(key, ...), and ValidationProblems.cs:13 then builds the dictionary from ModelState. Nothing in the repo documents or tests how ModelState stores a key. A likely explanation, which is framework behaviour outside the repo and NOT for the docs: ModelState keys are case-insensitive, and the route binder has already recorded an entry 'reference'. So AddModelError('REFERENCE') would land on that entry and come back as 'reference', while ?COLOUR would still give 'cOLOUR'. If that is right, no single casing rule covers client keys, which is why the doc cannot generalise from code. The 'so' is false on the repo's own evidence. The 400 comes from the filter's binding-source test (RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:12-17), not from casing, and lower-case ?reference=X gives the same 400 (RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:84-95). RECURRENCE: same paragraph and same cause as A2 I1 (asserting the casing of the ?REFERENCE key, and a reason for it, without proof). Only the claimed reason changed, from a naming policy to a code reading, so I reuse I1's fingerprint. WHY THE INV-003 ROUTE DID NOT PREVENT IT: (1) The A2 findings put the code prediction and 'rEFERENCE' into the builder's inputs. (2) inv-003 rec 4 (inv-003.plan.md:40, accepted) says to pin the casing with tests 'before any doc states it'. No bug plan exists (docs/plans/active holds only build and inv-001..003), yet the doc states a casing. (3) The rewritten brief (build.dag.yaml:356) says to report error keys 'as the code does it'. That invites a code reading. (4) inv-003 rec 1 (inv-003.plan.md:37) allows 'marked observed/untested' as an alternative to removal. claims.json:8 used that to keep a prediction that contradicts the only observation. (5) claims.json:512 records the sentence as 'A client-sent key keeps the rest of its casing; unknown query key ... is a 400', with a semicolon where design.md:72 has 'so'. The table paraphrased away the causal word that the check most needed to catch. FIX DIRECTION: replace the whole bullet at docs/design.md:70-76 with wording that states only what is tested or plainly in the code, with no prediction and no 'so'. EXACT REPLACEMENT: '- **Validation error keys.** For a body or model error, the API lower-cases the first letter of each dot-separated segment of the key (`ValidationProblems.cs`); for example, the key for a policyholder’s date of birth is `policyholders[0].dateOfBirth`. A query key that the action does not bind from the query string is a `400`, with `Unknown query parameter.` under that key in `errors`. A key named after a route parameter is one of these: `GET /policies/{reference}?reference=X` is a `400` keyed `reference`. No test sends a query key in upper case, so the key returned for one is not specified. The renewal endpoint with no body writes its key, `amount`, by hand in the controller.' SOURCES, one per sentence: (a) ValidationProblems.cs:15 and :25-26, and tests/postman/Uinsure.Policies.postman_collection.json:2278 asserts errors has 'policyholders[0].dateOfBirth'. (b) RejectUnknownQueryParametersFilter.cs:12-17 and :23-25, and RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:75-79 (colour, message). (c) RetrieveNotFoundTests.cs:90-94. (d) a grep of tests/ for an upper-case query key (pattern '\?[A-Z]{2,}[A-Za-z]*=' in *.cs and in the Postman collection) finds none. The 'so' in (d) rests on the absence of a test, which is provable, not on code behaviour. (e) PoliciesController.cs:91-95. Remove the '?REFERENCE', 'rEFERENCE' and 'keeps the rest of its casing' text, claims.json:512 and :518, and the rEFERENCE item in claims.json:8. If David wants the observation kept, the only allowed form is a standalone sentence: 'One manual check of `?REFERENCE=X` saw the key `reference` (`docs/qa/build-F2.md`).' Nothing may be joined to it by so, because or 'by the code'. A doc may state the casing of a client-sent key only after the rec-4 bug plan pins it.

(RetrieveNotFoundTests)

SYMPTOM: inv-003 rec 1 was implemented (256 claims), and A3 still finds a false 'so', widened scopes, wider quantifiers and wrong refs. CAUSE: the trace checks that a source exists and is relevant, not that it supports the exact sentence, for four reasons. (1) The 'sentence' field paraphrases instead of quoting, so the words the check needs go missing. claims.json:512 turns design.md:72's 'so' into ';', and claims.json:362 keeps 'All routes' but cites a narrower fact. (2) The sources cited sometimes disprove the sentence: requirements.md:125 for R2, commit-msg:33-45 for R3, PolicyService.cs:56-121 for R3. A source-supports-sentence check would have caught each. (3) inv-003 rec 1 allows 'marked observed/untested' as a way out. claims.json:8 used it to keep a code prediction that contradicts the only observation (I1). I14 was 'no trace step'; this is 'a trace step that checks presence, not support'. So it gets a new fingerprint, and the per-sentence recurrences in I1 and I2 carry the escalation. It asserts that each deploying-stage AzureCLI@2 step has the input keys azureSubscription, scriptType, scriptLocation and inlineScript (check-pipeline.py:83-86). So 'not checked' is false for task inputs, service connections, environments and `${{ }}` expressions, and true only in the sense 'not checked against Azure DevOps'. The next paragraph, infrastructure/README.md:77-79, already says so ('It does not validate those values against Azure DevOps'), so :74-75 and :77-79 contradict each other. So the table confirmed that the sentence matched the spec, not that it matched the checker. OBLIGATION: A6 requires an exact, bounded statement of what the schema check does not prove. Adding the missing qualifier keeps that obligation and makes each clause true. FIX DIRECTION: keep the A6 sentence and change only its end. findings.cause: A4 R4. WHAT THE SENTENCE SAYS: README.md:66 reads '**No £0 Refund record is created.** The cancellation response still lists every term with `refundAmount` 0.00.' With no comma and no qualifier, it says every term has 0.00. WHAT THE REPO PROVES: every term is listed. Policy.cs:257 calculates every term, Policy.cs:92 and :107 put all the calculations into the decision, and CancellationContracts.cs:23 returns the Terms list. Terms with an amount keep their amount (CancelRenewedPolicyTests.cs:68-69: 17.36 and 512.66). A term shows 0.00 only when its calculation is 0, and that is not limited to COULD-2 and UNPAID-TERM. A term that is already over is CANCEL-1c 0.00 with no refund (CancelRenewedPolicyTests.cs:88-89, :116 and :157). Read as exhaustive, it would leave out the CANCEL-1c 0.00 of a finished term, which would create a new overreach. This is truer than the reviewer's 'each such term', whose antecedent ('£0' in the bold clause) is weak. TRACE: update claims.json:274-278 to quote the new sentence. Source it to Policy.cs:257, Policy.cs:107, CancellationContracts.cs:23, Api CancelWithClaimTests.cs:47 and CancelRenewedPolicyTests.cs:116. Re-run the anchor check. findings.source: gate.red event at head 8d2bb50 in docs/trace/ui/U0b/loop.jsonl
findings.symptom: This is one cause, and it blocks all 11 rule greps (DATA-1, DATA-3, DATA-5, DATA-6, DATA-7, THEME-1, SEC-1, BRAND-1, HONEST-1, A11Y-1, RESP-1). I have deliberately kept it as one finding, filed under DATA-1, the first node rule. playwright.config.ts:1 does a named import of `defineConfig` from '@playwright/test', and Node throws a SyntaxError before any test is collected, so each grep reports 0 failed and 0 passed.
findings.cause: src/web/tsconfig.json:20-25 sets a catch-all `paths` mapping, "*" to ["./node_modules/@types/*", "./node_modules/*"]. Playwright's loader applies tsconfig `paths` to bare specifiers in .ts files (node_modules/playwright/lib/transform/esmLoader.js:7792-7826). So '@playwright/test' is rewritten to the directory src/web/node_modules/@playwright/test. That directory is then resolved with afterPathMapping=true (esmLoader.js:7619-7622), which looks only at `main` (absent) and then `index` with '.js' tried first (esmLoader.js:7597). The result is the CommonJS index.js, not the ESM index.mjs that the package's `exports.import` condition names (node_modules/@playwright/test/package.json:20). index.js:17 is `module.exports = require('playwright/test')`, and playwright/test.js:24 builds its exports with `Object.assign(...)`. Node's CJS named-export detection cannot see names built that way, so `defineConfig` is not a named export when an ES module (package.json:4 is "type": "module") imports it. Every spec and support file under tests/web/e2e/U0b/ named-imports `test`/`expect` from '@playwright/test' (for example data-1.spec.ts:4 and support/app.ts:7), so they would fail the same way. Changing only the config's import would fix the symptom, not the cause. The mapping exists so that tsc can resolve bare imports from tests/web/** (outside the package) to src/web/node_modules, and it was in the scaffold. gate.scaffold (0f2d3c6) ran typecheck and build but never loaded Playwright, so nothing caught it.
findings.fixDirection: the typecheck still needs to resolve tests/web/** imports to the package's node_modules, but Playwright's runtime must stop resolving package specifiers through this wildcard. Either Playwright loads under a tsconfig without the catch-all package mapping, or the mapping is narrowed so it no longer turns installed packages into directory paths, letting the package `exports` (import → .mjs) resolve. This is a scaffold-level config change in src/web/, not a test change. No test may be weakened.

findings.cause: the app itself switches theme on every fresh dark-system load. src/web/index.html:2 ships <html data-theme="light">. The token sheet's system-dark rule is scoped to :root:not([data-theme="light"]) (tokens.css:36-37), so that attribute switches it off, and the first paint is always light (tokens.css:22-34), whatever the system says. Only after React has mounted and painted does Frame.tsx:26-31 (useEffect, called at :57) set data-theme to 'dark' (Frame.tsx:29). The top bar's button and toggle are already in the DOM with light computed colours, so that change starts their 120ms fades from the light colours to the dark ones. Halfway through, the text and the fill are both mid-greys, which fails 4.5:1. The audit's readiness checks do not wait for the fades. The unbuilt page's check ('not built yet', a11y-1.spec.ts:72) is met on the first render, and the overview's footer stamp (a11y-1.spec.ts:51) one trace fetch later. So axe sometimes samples inside the 120ms window and sometimes after it. That is why the failure is intermittent, why it moves between routes, and why the overview passed 5/5 alone. The rest is my inference from the timing, not measured. Discriminator: in light, index.html:2 already says 'light' and Frame.tsx:29 writes 'light' again, so nothing changes and nothing fades. Every reported failure is dark, which fits. This breaks THEME-1, 'following the system setting' (docs/ui-requirements.md:184), at first paint, and a real dark-mode user sees a light flash and then a fade. A11Y-1's 'contrast in both themes' (docs/ui-requirements.md:183) fails during that window. The kit is not the cause. Its tokens already follow the system with no attribute (tokens.css:36-49), and its transitions are correct for a change the user makes. kitchen-sink.html:2 carries the same hard-coded light, but that is kit-owned and outside U0b. Evidence gap: run 1's axe message is not in the receipt (loop.jsonl:54 names the test only), and src/web/test-results/ holds only .last-run.json. That run 1 had the same cause is inferred from the same top bar being on every route, not proven. Why the earlier route didn't prevent it: this is the first fingerprint, with no match in A1, D1, A2 or A3. The web-tester saw a theme-toggle__face flag once at the A3 finding-red (its greps at activity.jsonl:804-807) but never filed it, and the six clean repeats were read as clearance. Repeats cannot clear a timing race. It probably became more frequent because of I3's fix. A2 I3 records that the old Frame.tsx swapped in an UnreadFrame, with no kit top bar, while the trace loaded. The top bar therefore mounted only after the theme had already switched, and inherited dark with no fade. The current Frame.tsx:94-98 renders the kit AppShell from the first commit, so the top bar now fades on every dark load. I took the old code from A2's description, not from that commit.

The first paint must already follow the system setting, so applying the choice after mount changes no colour on a normal load and starts no fade. The CSP (index.html:6, default-src 'self') rules out an inline pre-paint script. The test must not be bent to hide this: no reduced-motion emulation, and no waiting out the fades as the only change. Owner: web-builder (src/web/index.html and src/web/app/shell/Frame.tsx). No /kit-gap is needed.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the system emulated as dark before navigation, and an init script that records, from the moment the parser creates <html>, every value its data-theme attribute takes until the page is ready, When the overview opens on the complete fixture trail and its footer stamp shows, Then the recorded values never include 'light' and the last is 'dark'. (A new 'THEME-1 · on a fresh load the first theme the page shows follows the system setting, dark' in tests/web/e2e/U0b/theme-1.spec.ts, added in its own red commit by the web-tester. It is deterministic, not a race: index.html:2 parses with 'light' before any script runs, on every load. It turns green only when the first paint follows the system. Afterwards the existing A11Y-1 axe tests should pass on repeat, e.g. --repeat-each 10 at --workers=1, as supporting evidence only.)

findings.source: steer(D1,pause1)
findings.symptom: Layer note: the schema accepts only domain, services, persistence, api or tests, and has no web layer. This cause is in the web app's screen layer, at the app entry and shell, which is the presentation edge. It is filed as 'api' for that reason only. It is not the C# API and not a tests cause. on #/plans/ui/U0b/matrix and #/no-such-page, both of which fall to the catch-all route at src/web/app/shell/App.tsx:17 and render only the short NotBuiltYet box (src/web/app/shell/NotBuiltPage.tsx:7), the footer sits straight under that box and the bare page canvas shows below it.
findings.cause: the shell is built to fill the window and push the footer down. It is a flex column (src/web/kit/layouts/app-shell/AppShell.module.css:6-7), its <main> has `flex: 1 1 auto` (AppShell.module.css:40), and the shell's own height is `min-height: 100%` (AppShell.module.css:12). A percentage min-height needs a parent with a set height, and the app's document gives it none. src/web/index.html:2, :9 and :10 (html, body, #root) carry no height. The only stylesheet src/web/app/main.tsx:8 loads is the kit's tokens.css, which sets only custom properties and color-scheme on :root (src/web/kit/tokens/tokens.css:2-63), with no html, body or #root rule. Repo-wide, the only height rule on that path is AppShell.module.css:12. So the 100% works out to auto, the shell is only as tall as its content, and main's flex-grow has no spare space to fill. The overview, about and activity screens are taller than the window, which hides the defect there. Only short routes show it, and that covers every not-built route. The derived references and the stylekit have the same gap (docs/ui/stylekit/kit.css:4173 `min-height: 100%`, and no html or body rule in docs/ui/stylekit/), so parity checks will not catch it. Interpretation: RESP-1 says the app is 'designed for 1440 and 1280 wide'. The kit's AppShell comment (AppShell.tsx:22-26) describes a page frame of top bar, nav, main and footer. A footer floating mid-window on a laptop-height window breaks that frame. No requirements row names footer placement, so RESP-1 is the closest rule, not an exact one.
findings.fixDirection: the page's host document (the app entry, not the kit, which a build node never changes) must give the chain from html through body to #root the window's height, so the kit's percentage min-height has a set parent to resolve against. The body's default margin should go at the same time, so the filled frame fits the window exactly and doesn't scroll by a few pixels. If the orchestrator rules that the kit's own `min-height: 100%` is the defect instead, that is a kit change, to be stopped and reported to David, not patched in a screen.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the app served on the complete fixture trail at 1440x900 and at 1280x800, in light and dark, When the page opens #/no-such-page and #/plans/ui/U0b/matrix (both not-built routes, whose content is shorter than the window), Then the footer's box ends within 1px of the window's bottom edge, the document is no taller than the window, and nothing shows below the footer; and on #/ (taller than the window) the footer still follows the content. Tag it 'RESP-1 · on a short page the footer sits at the bottom of the window'. (tests/web/e2e/U0b/resp-1.spec.ts, Playwright)

findings.source: docs/trace/ui/U1/loop.jsonl:28 gate.coverage (render-trace check ui U1 --stage gates, exit 1, head 9b82b4b): 640e3e1 has no activity record for Agent web-builder
findings.symptom: The gate is a harness check, not a node rule, so no layer in the schema's enum fits. 'tests' is used because the harness self-test is the test home. AGENT-2 is the nearest rule, because it reads activity.jsonl. What happened: the commit landed. The worktree reflog (.git/worktrees/ui-U1/logs/HEAD:31) has 640e3e1 at 1792615730, which is 20:48:50Z. Yet web-builder a022182fa89499cd2 has no record between activity.jsonl:569 (Edit at 20:43:24Z) and :570 (20:49:34Z). There is no typecheck, no test run, no git add and no git commit in that window. Its first call afterwards, `git log -1 …; git status` (:570) followed by `git rev-parse HEAD` (:571), is a check on whether its commit had landed, which fits its report that hooks blocked some of its Bash calls. The cause is that the trail records tool calls only from trace-activity, and trace-activity runs only on PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure (settings.json:73-96). A call denied by a PreToolUse guard exits 2 (io.mjs:11-14; guard-bash.mjs:490, guard-agent.mjs:74/81) and never reaches trace-activity. A trace-activity run that is killed (5 s timeout, settings.json:80) or that throws writes only to stderr (trace-activity.mjs:82-83). So the trail holds no record of any hook outcome. The hook itself works when its Post event completes: every other commit on this node got a record 6-7 s after its reflog time (feb65db 20:12:48 → activity.jsonl:438 at 20:12:55; dab4975 20:40:24 → :551 at 20:40:31; 0aa060b 20:51:05 → :582 at 20:51:11). The trail cannot show which mechanism dropped the call that did commit. One candidate is a Post hook killed at its 5 s budget under the parallel W1 and KG4 Playwright load (loop.jsonl:16). The other is a PreToolUse guard timing out and failing open, which would let the command run while the builder saw a hook error. Both are claims, not evidence, and that missing evidence is the cause itself. It recurs: this is the same class as build/F1 762c994 (build/F1/loop.jsonl:55, :60). That fix added PostToolUseFailure, which covers only a call that ran and exited non-zero. It does not cover denials, hook timeouts or a killed Post hook. U0b's four lost records (ui/U0b/loop.jsonl:42-48) were backfilled with no change on the capture side. Both earlier routes treated the symptom.
findings.fixDirection: (a harness change, so it goes through a harness/<slug> PR, never this node, because of the harness lock) make every hook outcome on a node branch leave a durable trail record. That means a denial record from the PreToolUse guards (agent, agent_id, tool_use_id, redacted command, reason) and a mark when trace-activity fails or is cut short. Also keep the commit-recording path well inside its timeout, so load cannot silently drop a commit record.
findings.suggestedTest: Given a node branch fixture and a subagent Bash call (agent_id set, agent_type web-builder) that guard-bash or guard-agent denies, When the guard runs and exits 2, Then the node's activity.jsonl gains one record with that agent_id, tool_use_id, the redacted command and the deny reason; and Given trace-activity's commit path on a commit call, When it runs, Then it completes inside its configured timeout (guards.test.mjs / trace.test.mjs, node --test)

findings.source: docs/trace/ui/U1/loop.jsonl:28 gate.coverage (render-trace check ui U1 --stage gates, exit 1, head 9b82b4b): 640e3e1 has no activity record for Agent web-builder
findings.symptom: The gate is a harness check, so 'tests' is used here for the same reason as I1. The check is honest about the symptom but not about the gap. render-trace.mjs:163-164 asks only whether a commit has a matching activity record. That catches 640e3e1, but it would never notice the builder's missing test runs or its blocked calls. The only exit is reconciledFor (render-trace.mjs:159-162). It accepts any reconciled(activity:<sha7>) event whose detail is non-empty. The tool that writes that event, backfill-activity (render-trace.mjs:418-425), writes agent_id null, tool null and command null, plus a fixed detail: 'the activity record read from git'. Run on 640e3e1, it would turn gate.coverage OK while dropping four facts the trail holds or could hold. First, which dispatched agent made the commit (a022182fa89499cd2, whose other calls are at activity.jsonl:553-571). Second, that its calls from 20:43:24Z to 20:48:50Z (reflog) are missing, not merely the commit. Third, that hooks denied some of its calls. Fourth, that the cause is not known. That breaks DATA-4's agreed interpretation ('Incomplete is never clean') and HONEST-1 (no status that isn't in the trail, which can't be waived). F1's reconciled(activity:0e4fe2f) (build/F1/loop.jsonl:60) carried its cause only because it was written by hand. U0b's backfills (ui/U0b/loop.jsonl:45-48) carry only the generic text, so the earlier route already let a lost record pass with no cause stated.
findings.fixDirection: a reconciliation for a lost agent record should carry the evidence, not just exist. That means the agent session id when the trail can attribute it, the window with no records, the commit time from git, and the agent's own report of blocked calls labelled as a claim. The check should refuse a reconciled(activity:…) event whose detail lacks them, rather than accepting any non-empty detail. For this node, the honest route is a backfill that names a022182fa89499cd2, the 20:43:24Z-20:48:50Z window and the unexplained cause. A generic backfill would hide all three.
findings.suggestedTest: Given a fixture trail whose web-builder commit has no activity record while the same agent_id has earlier records, and a reconciled(activity:<sha7>) event whose detail is the generic 'read from git' text with no agent id or window, When render-trace check runs, Then it reports TRAIL INCOMPLETE naming the commit; and Given the same event carrying the agent id, the unrecorded window and the commit time, Then the commit reason clears (trace.test.mjs, node --test)

findings.source: docs/trace/ui/U1/loop.jsonl line 10, steer(D1,pause1)
findings.symptom: Layer note: the real layer is the compiler, one of the ui plan's layers (compiler, loader, client, screen). The gate-subagent schema accepts only domain|services|persistence|api|tests, so 'services' stands in here. That mismatch between the investigator brief and the hook is a harness gap. the FAILs-taken figure that D1 gave to U1 is built from an incomplete verdicts[] on the real trail, and every valid re-review verdict is wrongly listed in problems[].
findings.cause: src/web/compiler/index.ts:89 reads the round from the file name with /\/(A\d+)-([^/]+)\.json$/. That pattern accepts only A<n>-<agent>.json, but the orchestrator names a same-attempt re-review A<n>.<m>-<agent>.json. So verdictOf returns null at index.ts:91, and index.ts:211 files the verdict as 'the verdict file is not a verdict' instead of pushing it at :212. On docs/trace at HEAD, 22 of the 57 verdict files use the A<n>.<m> form (build/F0b, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6 and ui/U0b). For the build plan the compiler emits 31 of 51 verdicts and 8 of 9 FAILs: it drops docs/trace/build/F5/verdicts/A2.4-reviewer.json (FAIL). That breaks NAV-1 ('attempts and FAILs taken ... from the data') and HONEST-1 (a number that isn't the trail's). U3's LOOP-3 builds on these same records, and its kit already renders 'A3.2' rounds (verdict-card, attempt-ladder), so U3 would inherit the defect. It went undetected because every fixture trail names only A1 and A2 rounds, and nav-1.test.ts:68-79 asserts only those. This is a first diagnosis, not a recurrence of A1's harness cause. It will fire on every future re-review round until the round form is accepted. The rest of the D1 resolution checks clean. data-1.test.ts:84-97 drops only the verdicts assertion, as the steer ruled, and its comment now names U1 as the owner. No test still asserts that verdicts stay empty. docs/ui-requirements.md:418 and ui.dag.yaml:155,178-179 keep U3's LOOP-3 rendering of verdicts, which doesn't conflict with U1 owning the list.
findings.fixDirection: treat the round as the whole A<n>[.<m>] token in the file name, and keep it verbatim as the round string (e.g. 'A2.2'), so that a re-review verdict is parsed like any other and no valid verdict reaches problems[]. Then add a fixture case with a re-review round, so the compiler test proves this form.
findings.suggestedTest: Given a fixture trail whose node has verdicts A1-reviewer.json FAIL, A1-security.json PASS, A1.2-reviewer.json PASS and A1.2-security.json PASS, in the real envelope cut from docs/trace/build/F3/verdicts/A2.2-reviewer.json (a new fixture, or added to the rules fixture with its README figures updated), When the compiler runs, Then verdicts[] holds all four with rounds A1, A1, A1.2, A1.2, their agents, verdicts and files, and problems[] names no verdict file ('NAV-1 · FAILs taken: a re-review round A<n>.<m> is a verdict, not a problem' in tests/web/unit/compiler/nav-1.test.ts)

findings.cause: src/web/compiler/git.ts:46 turns the trailer lines into a map with Object.fromEntries, so a key that appears twice keeps only its last value. The type at git.ts:11 (Record<string, string>) can't hold a repeated key in any case. Evidence that the real trail has repeated keys: F1's domain green commit has seven Rule lines, SELL-1 to SELL-7 (docs/trace/build/F1/packet/trailers.txt:420-431, and the api green at :511-522). Those are the packet's pre-rewrite SHAs (727fcc3, 7b3ebb3). Their subjects match docs/trace/build/F1/walkthrough.md:57 (row 52, 7d3f791) and :69 (row 64, f6c64dd). I had no shell to run git log on 7d3f791 itself; the t12 tester's confirmation at loop.jsonl:58 is a claim. Downstream, the collapsed value is read at index.ts:157 and split at index.ts:165, which handles only the comma form. ruleFacts.ts:56 then filters the spine with commit.rule.includes(rule.id), and Commit.tsx:61-62 draws one chip per entry. Other readers of a repeated trailer: (a) Fixes-Finding, index.ts:167. Repeated Fixes-Finding lines are common in the real trail, so all but the last are lost: build/F1 packet trailers.txt:169-175 has seven lines, F6 :102-114 has thirteen, and F2, F3, F1b and F0b have them too. No U1 screen reads fixesFinding (no match in src/web/app). (b) The DATA-5 privacy scan, index.ts:154, scans Object.values(commit.trailers). Today an earlier repeated value is dropped before the scan and also never emitted, so nothing leaks. Once the fix emits every value, the scan must see every value, or a denylisted earlier line will reach trace.json. A separate cause, not filed as a finding because no U1 screen reads it: index.ts:78 parses only A<n>/<id>, so the real D<n>/I<n> values (F1 packet :115 and onwards) compile with round null. It is for U3. Why no test caught this: the fixture format can't express a repeated key. replay.mjs:48 builds the trailer block from a JSON object (README.md:14), and data-5.test.ts:121 does the same, so every fixture commit has at most one line per key. data-1.test.ts:80-81 covers only the comma form. Recurrence: new cause, so it gets a new fingerprint. It is the same class as D1/I1 and D2/I1: a compiler shape narrower than the real trail, and a hand-cut fixture that leaves the real shape out. The D2 round's check of 'commit parents … on real git: parse correctly' (D2.md previous_attempts) didn't look at repeated keys, so it didn't prevent this.
findings.fixDirection: the trailer reader keeps every value of a key, in order. Rule and Fixes-Finding are the union of every line, each line also split on commas. The privacy scan covers every value of every key. The single-valued trailers (Agent, Plan, Node, TDD) keep a stated rule for a repeat, never a silent last-wins.

findings.symptom: the LOOP-1 axe test passes on the stub, whose content is canned.
findings.cause: the test's only check that the page is drawing the trail is the ready callback at tests/web/e2e/U3/loop-1.spec.ts:203. That callback waits for gateRow(region(p, TIMELINE), FAIL.name) to be visible. gateRow (tests/web/e2e/U3/support/app.ts:55-56) matches by accessible name only, so it waits for '1·4 gate.stub: Gate failed' (loop-1.spec.ts:48). The kit builds that name from marker, gate and result alone (src/web/kit/project/gate-row/GateRow.tsx:59, `${marker} ${gate}: ${word}`, with 'failed' mapped to 'Gate failed' at :40). The stub's canned row is design-fixture build/F3, which also failed gate.stub at attempt 1, line 4: src/web/app/explorer/loop/Loop.tsx:46 renders marker='1·4', gate='gate.stub', result='failed'. So the canned row has exactly the same accessible name as the retry-ladder fixture's F1 line 4 (tests/web/fixtures/trails/retry-ladder/trail/docs/trace/build/F1/loop.jsonl:4). The two trails coincide on that name, so the guard holds on canned content. After the guard, auditEverywhere (tests/web/e2e/U1/support/app.ts:166-177) checks only the theme token and axe. Neither depends on the data, so the canned page passes. The spec already has the right kind of guard, used by every other LOOP-1 behaviour test: openTimeline at loop-1.spec.ts:64-68 waits for detail text that only the fixture's line 4 holds ('the stub throws on a reference it has answered'), and Loop.tsx has none of it. The axe test skips openTimeline and uses the weaker name check, both on its first open (:201) and inside the callback. The other four U3 axe tests guard on fixture-only values: data-2.spec.ts:105 the compiled snapshot short SHA, loop-2.spec.ts:201, loop-3.spec.ts:215, loop-4.spec.ts:185. Only this one keys on a value that the design fixture and the behaviour fixture share. The stub is not at fault. It renders the derived reference as canned kit JSX, as the web-testing stub step requires. Changing its canned content to dodge the guard would fit the stub to the test, and a later stub could match by chance again.
findings.fixDirection: (tests, web-tester) the axe test's ready callback should wait for a value only the retry-ladder trail produces, as openTimeline does. Examples: line 4's verbatim detail, or the link to the compiled fixture's c2 SHA, which differs on each compile. That way, every one of the four theme and width loads is proven to draw the trail before axe runs. This tightens the guard and weakens nothing. It is still a change to a test after its red commit, so it should land as its own tests commit and be re-gated: red first, then re-run gate.stub at edc078a, where it must now fail. Not a recurrence: this is the node's first finding. Attempt 1's red gate (loop.jsonl:3, b8ee2c6) could not catch it, because no route existed at red and every test failed for that reason. A guard that canned content can satisfy only shows up once a stub renders the reference.

Also, :238 'if (name in found) return' skips a repeated marker's segment, and that marker's index still ends the first segment, so the text after the repeat goes nowhere. compiler/index.ts:284 stores only the three fields, with no verbatim root_cause, and Finding.tsx:84-87 renders only those three fields, so the page has nothing to fall back on. The signed-off reference already decides the preamble case. docs/ui/derived/U3/finding/long-content.html:33 says 'Where a sentence comes before the "Symptom:" marker, it opens the Symptom field', and :61, :65, :73 and :77 draw D2 I7, I8, I10 and I11 that way. findings.fixDirection: a marker counts as a split point only where it opens the text or a sentence and is not inside a quotation. A quoted marker stays as words in the field around it. The word check in the tests must strip only the real split markers. Already done: the red commit 55e5364 adds four tests (loop-4.test.ts:305-346), including U3's real A3 text. The fix 3b25c3c adds opensASentence (plans.ts:231-237) as a filter on the marks (:245-247), and gate.test at 3b25c3c shows 304 passed (loop.jsonl:96). Not covered: opensASentence counts double quotes, backticks and curly quotes but not single quotes, because those are ambiguous with apostrophes. A marker that opens a sentence inside a multi-sentence single-quoted span would still split. I did not check the trail for that shape. Recurrence: new fingerprint, but it is the third round of the same class as A2 and A3. The A3 route turned 'every character lands in a field' into a test oracle that stripped marker names anywhere, so the oracle shared the code's assumption that a marker name is always a marker. findings.symptom: This is reviewer R1 (P1). RULING (David, delegated): U3 lands with R1 as tech debt. Its fix belongs to U7, line docs/plans/active/ui.dag.yaml:453, committed at 77f25aa, and not to this node. The layer is the ui compiler. It is recorded as 'api' because the layer enum has no ui value, as in A2 to A4. on U3's own D1/I1 finding page, about 1,800 characters of preamble show as Symptom, the text after 'Done.
findings.cause: x' shows as Cause, and Fix direction is empty. opensASentence (src/web/compiler/plans.ts:232-237) treats a quotation as open by counting only double quotes, backticks and curly quotes (:236). A straight single quote is never counted, so a marker after a sentence end inside a single-quoted span passes both checks. It passes the sentence-start test at :234 because 'Done. ' ends in '. ', and it passes the quote test at :236 because there are no double quotes before it. The filter at :245-247 then keeps it as a split point. D1's root_cause (docs/trace/ui/U3/findings/D1.md:14) has exactly this shape. Its other quoted markers ('Symptom:', 'Cause:', 'Fix direction:') come mid-sentence, so :234 already drops them. 'The cause:' is lower case and does not match :245. That leaves the single-quoted 'Done. x' as the only mark. Every finding goes through this function (src/web/compiler/index.ts:284). Leaving single quotes out was deliberate: D1's own text has apostrophes ('function's', 'code's', 'LOOP-4/DATA-2's'), so counting single quotes the same way would unbalance on the first apostrophe. The fix at 3b25c3c covered only the quote characters that cannot be apostrophes. Rule: LOOP-4 shows symptom, cause and fix direction as the investigator recorded them, and DATA-2 says recorded means verbatim. A4/I1's fix direction says a marker that is inside a quotation is not a split point.
findings.fixDirection: (for U7, not U3) count a straight single quote as a quotation mark only at a word boundary. It opens after the start of the text, white space or an opening bracket, and closes before white space or punctuation. A single quote between two letters is an apostrophe and does not change the quote state. A marker inside an open single-quoted span stays words in the field around it. Tests: loop-4.test.ts:305-346 cover double-quoted and mid-sentence shapes only. None covers a sentence-start marker inside single quotes, and none covers an apostrophe in the same text. Recurrence: same cause as A4/I1, a quoted marker treated as a split point, now with straight single quotes. The fingerprint is reused on purpose. D1/I1 named this exact gap as 'Not covered'. The 3b25c3c route fixed the shapes its four tests named, and the oracle that strips nothing (:297) was sound, but no fixture held a single-quoted multi-sentence span. David's ruling settles the escalation, so this reuse is meant as a record, not as another climb up the retry ladder.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the retry-ladder trail with A2/I1's root_cause set to "Symptom: S1. Cause: the round's text says 'Done. Cause: x' and keeps the function's contract. Fix direction: F1.", When the compiler runs, Then the symptom is 'S1.', the cause is "the round's text says 'Done. Cause: x' and keeps the function's contract." word for word, and the fix direction is 'F1.'. A second case uses D1/I1's real root_cause text, and its whole text lands in the cause with no fix direction (tests/web/unit/compiler/loop-4.test.ts, a U7 red test)

The D1 route closes that gap with an oracle that strips nothing. findings.cause: x'. No test covers this. (2) Three things on the regression gate. gate.e2e-regression at 3b25c3c is ok:false (loop.jsonl:99), and its detail holds only NO_COLOR warnings. findings.symptom: [ui layer: screen, mapped to 'api'.] First of two causes behind R5, split on purpose (see I7). the rule page's printed expectation can be false for a sound trail.
findings.cause: src/web/app/explorer/rule/Rule.tsx:231 prints `git log --reverse ... ${red}^..${green}`, and :235 promises red first and green last. When a merge lands between red and green, as U4's own merge of origin/ui (eddb436) did, the range red^..green also holds the merged branch's commits. Those are reachable from green but not from red^. With --reverse, the ones older than red are listed before red, so 'red first' fails. 'green last' still holds, because green is the tip. The green..refactor command at :245 only promises refactor last, which holds. Rule: VERIFY-1, 'the git command that re-checks it without the UI'; a command whose stated expectation doesn't hold re-checks nothing.
findings.fixDirection: the command and its expectation must agree whenever merges sit in the range. Either list only the node branch's own line of commits, or state an expectation that is true with merges present. Kit components: none (the text is the app's).
findings.suggestedTest: Given a fixture trail whose rule has a merge commit between its red and green, the merged branch holding a commit older than red (a new fixture in the red commit), When the test runs the rule page's printed verify command in that fixture's repo, Then the output's first line is the red with trailer red and its last line is the green with trailer green, as the page says (tests/web/e2e/U4/verify-1.spec.ts).

findings.symptom: The cause is in the test, not the screens. I1 and I4 share it. the 'POST /api/policies is answered' poll timed out after 5000 ms. The screen behaved as it should. error-context.md lines 209-210 for this test show the Sell button as 'Selling…' [disabled] with the status 'In flight: POST /policies. Waiting for the API to answer.' The page-sends poll at workbench.ts:369 passed, so the request left the page. The API did not answer inside the 5 s default of expect.poll at workbench.ts:371: playwright.config.ts:6-17 sets no expect timeout and nothing warms the API. This test (a11y-1.spec.ts:39-43, W1-AXE-1) is the first test in the first spec file. With 2 workers and no fullyParallel, Playwright gives one file to each worker, so this was worker 1's first live sale through the preview proxy. W1-AXE-3 at a11y-1.spec.ts:55-59 runs the same sell-and-answer flow later in the same worker and passed. The node's own discarded run (10 workers starved the API, UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT) shows this API is slow under concurrent cold load. Not recoverable from the artifacts: which hop stalled (cold API, first POST through the proxy). playwright.config.ts keeps no trace, so only error-context.md exists.
findings.fixDirection: the first live round trip of each worker must not race a 5 s default. Either warm the API and proxy path before the first behaviour test, or give the waits that depend on the API a timeout sized for a live API. Turn on trace retention on failure so the next stall can be located. This makes the wait honest. It does not weaken the assertion. The orchestrator or David should confirm that it isn't counted as weakening a red test.
findings.untestableReason: The defect is in the acceptance test's own waiting, not in a behaviour under a rule. The existing test reproduces it as the first test of a worker on a cold API (npm --prefix src/web run e2e -- tests/web/e2e/W1 --workers=2 on a just-started API). findings.symptom: The cause is in the test, not the screens. at 'the dark theme's tokens are in force at 1440' the test read #ffffff instead of #1b1d21, with System checked. auditEverywhere (a11y-1.spec.ts:31-33) switches the theme in place: setTheme only calls page.emulateMedia (app.ts:114-116). The test then reads --color-background once, straight away. On the light pass Frame.tsx:31 has already written data-theme="light". tokens.css:36-37 gives the dark values under prefers-color-scheme: dark only to :root:not([data-theme="light"]), so the background stays #ffffff until the matchMedia 'change' listener (Frame.tsx:30-35) runs and rewrites data-theme as 'dark'. The screen does follow the system setting (THEME-1). U0b avoids the race in two ways: reloading after setTheme (U0b/a11y-1.spec.ts:40-44), or waiting for data-theme before reading (U0b/theme-1.spec.ts:83-84).
findings.fixDirection: after each theme switch, wait until the switch has taken effect (the attribute, or the token itself) before checking the token and running axe.
findings.untestableReason: The defect is in the acceptance test's own synchronisation. The existing test reproduces it when repeated (playwright test --grep "A11Y-1 · " --repeat-each=10). The product's theme behaviour is already covered and passing in U0b/theme-1.spec.ts.

findings.symptom: Layer note: the real ui layer is the screen, and the cause is the node's scope. 'api' stands in only because the hook's enum has no ui layer (gate-subagent.mjs takes domain|services|persistence|api|tests, while the investigator brief names compiler, loader, client and screen for a ui node). This is a scope problem. The screen code is a symptom, and the cause is not a gap in W1's tests. The hypothesis holds, with one addition. The symptom: Renew.tsx:6-8, :25-38 and :48-59 render F4-MVFJSC6LXX, the 2027-09-18..2027-10-18 window and a 2026-10-19..2027-10-18 term at 384.29. QuoteCancel.tsx:26 renders 'Cancel on 2026-12-02'. RecordClaim.tsx:15 renders 'answered 201'. Their buttons (Renew.tsx:68, QuoteCancel.tsx:25-28, RecordClaim.tsx:34) have no handler and are never busy. The cause: derive-screens.mjs:170-173 counts a region as built when any one of its rule IDs belongs to a built node. W1 owns the cross-cutting rules WB-2, WB-3 and BUSY-1 (ui.dag.yaml:296). So derived.json:55-110 marks as built for W1 the problem and busy regions of wb-cancel, wb-claim and wb-renew, and also wb-renew's 'the new term, last on the timeline' (req WB-5 WB-2, which the reviewer didn't list). Those screens' own work belongs to W2 (WB-4, ui.dag.yaml:327-332) and W3 (WB-5, ui.dag.yaml:361-366). Three steps then each took a different scope. (a) t2 (ui.dag.yaml:313) followed the derived reference: it registered all six routes (routes.tsx:22-24) and wrote canned content for them. (b) t1 (ui.dag.yaml:312, 'parity with its derived reference') narrowed parity to three screens (parity.ts:23 types the screen as 'wb-home' | 'wb-sell' | 'wb-policy'), and no W1 spec visits /cancel, /renew or /claims/new (a grep of tests/web/e2e/W1 finds none). (c) t6 (ui.dag.yaml:317) names only the home, sell and policy screens. So nothing could fail on these routes, the canned values from t2 survived to green, and gate.no-stubs (loop.jsonl:27) greps only for 'not implemented'. The routes are also reachable from the built screen: PolicyView.tsx:168 and :184 link to /cancel and /claims/new. HONEST-1 (MUST, can't be waived) says placeholder data 'is labelled as such and never ships'.
findings.fixDirection: David rules the scope first. Either W1 builds those regions against the live API, which pulls in W2's and W3's requests, or a cross-cutting rule's region on a screen whose main node isn't built is treated as not built. That second option is a derivation change in harness-locked .claude/scripts and needs David. After the ruling, the three screens show only what the API returned or the kit's not-built state, and the tests cover whatever scope is chosen. Recurrence: no fingerprint from A1 repeats, so this is new to the node. It is the same class as inv-001 (canned values survived because nothing told them apart). That route didn't prevent it because inv-001's remedies were orchestrator brief checks on build/F2, and no ui gate compares a node's derived reference against the screens its tests visit.

findings.symptom: Reviewer R3. Layer note: this is the web client (src/web/app/data/api.ts), not the C# API. 'api' is the closest allowed value, the same convention A1/I5 used. The hypothesis holds, with one refinement. the request log cannot show the exact exchange the signed-off reference shows. docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-requests/populated.html:33 draws 'Request headers (6)' and 'Response headers (4)' inside http-exchange, and the recordings carry both header sets (docs/ui/fixture/api/070-could-2-claim-dated-today-201.json:13-22, :45-51).
findings.cause: the data model. LoggedExchange has five fields and no headers (src/web/app/data/api.ts:368-374). loggingFetch stores the request body parsed (:393-400, :408) and the response as response.clone().json() (:415-418), so the wire text is gone before anything renders. Downstream, RequestLogPage gives HttpExchange no headers and re-stringifies the bodies (src/web/app/workbench/requests/RequestLogPage.tsx:68-80, :84), and the drawer pretty-prints the parsed body (src/web/app/workbench/RequestsDrawer.tsx:11). The kit is not the gap: it accepts request and response headers and an exact-text body (src/web/kit/patterns/http-exchange/HttpExchange.tsx:17-19, :29-31) and draws the disclosures only when headers are passed (:120-124, :136-140). Refinement: the builder didn't merely follow a stub. The red unit test pins the headerless, parsed shape with toEqual on exactly five keys and a parsed requestBody (tests/web/unit/client/wb-7.test.ts:20-22, :41). Gate.red passed typecheck with this type stubbed by the tester (loop.jsonl:3). A builder adding headers or raw text would have turned those red-committed tests red. No WB-7 test could catch the gap. The e2e compares String(leaf) with toContainText (tests/web/e2e/W3/wb-7.spec.ts:15-20, :56-57), which never looks at headers and cannot tell 100 from 100.00, and parity compares data-comp structure only. I did not run the API to confirm the reviewer's '100.00 becomes 100' example; the missing headers are enough to establish the finding on their own. Not raised by the reviewer and not merged here, only noted: RequestLogPage passes no curl, so the reference's 'Repeat it' part (populated.html:33; HttpExchange.tsx:154-158) is also missing. Origin: the red commits ac94134/75f3244 (type and pinned test). The A1 route did not touch api.ts or wb-7.test.ts (loop.jsonl:7: finding-red diff = tests/web/e2e/W3/** only; e795f19 changed only the amount default in RenewPolicy.tsx). Not a recurrence.
findings.fixDirection: tester first. Change the WB-7 red tests so the log entry must hold the request headers the client set, the response headers the API served, and both bodies as the exact text that went over the wire, and add an e2e assertion that the opened exchange shows a response-headers disclosure holding the exchange's content-type. This changes red-committed assertions in wb-7.test.ts. It strengthens them, but the orchestrator should record it as such. Then the builder: the logged exchange should carry headers and raw text, and the log page and drawer should pass them to the kit unchanged. One limit to state in the test: a browser's fetch cannot see the headers the browser adds itself (user-agent, host), so 'exact' means what the page set and what it received, not Postman's six. Routes to: tester (red), then builder. The tester alone cannot fix it.

findings.source: docs/trace/ui/W3/loop.jsonl gate.e2e (attempt 3, head 6f7a385, ok:false): wb-2.spec.ts:280 x2, wb-2.spec.ts:306, wb-3.spec.ts:208
findings.symptom: The layer is react-web's screen layer. The schema's enum has no screen value, so 'api' is used as the nearest edge layer; this routes to web-builder, not to the C# API. wb-2.spec.ts:306 (tokens only) times out on its region-count poll. The same extra region also keeps :280 x2 and wb-3.spec.ts:208 red after I1's settle is in.
findings.cause: src/web/app/workbench/policy/PolicyView.tsx:396 nests <NotBuiltRegion region="quote-and-cancel">, and NotBuiltRegion renders a section with data-region (src/web/app/shell/Rung.tsx:34). This adds a tenth [data-region] that no reference has: no file under docs/ui/ has data-region="quote-and-cancel", and both the W1 and W3 wb-policy references have 9 regions (docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-policy/populated.html:22-90). W1's tokens check polls regions.length against the reference's (tests/web/e2e/W1/support/parity.ts:234), so 10 never equals 9, and a settle does not change that count. 'quote-and-cancel' is not in either derived.json, so a U1-style regionSettled treats it as settled, and the order and unbuilt comparisons still see an entry the reference lacks. Second, the actions region carries data-req="WB-5" (PolicyView.tsx:386), but the signed-off reference tags it "WB-4 WB-5" (docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-policy/populated.html:75), against react-web's rule that 'each region's data-req IDs [are] kept'. This is a screen-composition defect: the screen invents a region. It does not break W1 behaviour (W1's flow tests passed in this gate).
findings.fixDirection: (route: web-builder) the page must have exactly the reference's regions. Keep showing the unbuilt quote-and-cancel action as not built yet (HONEST-1), but inside the actions region and without a data-region of its own, and give the actions region the reference's data-req. If the kit has no not-built pattern without a region, stop and report it as a kit gap; do not patch it in the screen.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the policy view opened on the recorded read-back with the design fixture's trace, When its [data-region] elements are read, Then they are exactly the nine slugs of docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-policy/populated.html in that order, none is 'quote-and-cancel', and the actions region's data-req is 'WB-4 WB-5' (a W3 wb-policy parity test in tests/web/e2e/W3/, as in I3)

findings.source: steer(D1,pause1)
findings.symptom: About the layer field: the stop hook only accepts domain|services|persistence|api|tests. My agent brief gives a ui node the layers compiler|loader|client|screen, and the hook rejects those. The true layer here is the kit, which the screen layer consumes. I chose 'tests' because the outcome was a change to a test line; the cause is not in the tests. The brief and the hook disagree, and that is a harness issue. U7 could not build the original SEC-1 line, which asked for rel=noreferrer on every link out.
findings.cause: the kit components that render the links out set no rel, and their props have no way to pass one in. Footer.tsx:53 renders the repository link as <a className href={repoHref}> with no rel. FooterProps (Footer.tsx:6-22) has no rel member. ShaLink.tsx:45-51 (the primary GitHub link when href is absent) and ShaLink.tsx:61 (the separate GitHub icon link) also have no rel, and ShaLinkProps (ShaLink.tsx:12-25) can't carry one. The fix belongs in src/web/kit/, and the react-web contract says the kit is 'consumed, never changed by a build node'. So no U7 green could make the four per-link tests on Footer and ShaLink pass. That is a kit gap, not a screen defect. The app's own links already set rel (Matrix.tsx:66,80; Rule.tsx:202,251,270), as does the kit's MarkdownText.tsx:167. The only links left without rel are the Footer and ShaLink ones. They are carried past the demo by the amended acceptance line (ui.dag.yaml:418). Recurrence: none. This is attempt 1 and the first D round, and no earlier attempt on U7 touched SEC-1 links.
findings.fixDirection: a kit change, through a kit-gap node, that adds rel=noreferrer to the Footer and ShaLink external anchors. U7 makes no change for this.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the Footer with a repoHref, and a ShaLink with a githubHref (with and without href), When they render, Then every anchor whose href points to github.com has a rel that includes noreferrer (tests/web/kit/, Testing Library; the kit's own tests, written in the kit-gap node, not a build node)

findings.source: steer(D1,pause1)

findings.cause: the in-node kit-gap renderer refuses any node id that isn't KG<n>. screens-fill.mjs:104 defines KIT_GAP = /^KG[1-9]\d*$/, and screens-fill.mjs:113 throws 'only a kit-gap node (KG<n>) renders here' when node is anything else, so passing node=U7 fails before any render. That leaves a build node two options: open a separate KG node, or carry the gap. The orchestrator carried it, and logged it as a harness bug at loop.jsonl:4. Recurrence: not from an earlier U7 attempt. It is a known, carried harness issue ('harness bug, carried', loop.jsonl:4), so a later node that needs an in-node kit gap will hit it again with this same fingerprint.
findings.fixDirection: (harness, David's call) either let the in-node kit-gap path run under a build node's id, or make the hand-off to a KG<n> node explicit. Subagents may not write .claude/, so this is outside U7.
findings.suggestedTest: Given screensFill called with node='U7' and screen='kit-layouts', When it runs, Then the behaviour matches the harness ruling: it either renders the gap feedback or names the KG<n> hand-off, instead of throwing at line 113 (.claude/hooks/__tests__ harness self-test, node --test)

That covers each directive sec-1.spec.ts:54-57 asserts, and the meta that sec-1.spec.ts:37-44 accepts. All three directives take effect when delivered by meta: browsers ignore only frame-ancestors, report-uri and sandbox in a meta CSP. Unlike per-link rel, it is a page-wide setting that any later index.html change could drop. The per-link line is carried, not dropped. (b) The react-web skill's SEC-1 bullet ('Links out … with rel="noreferrer"') still states the per-link form, so the skill and the amended acceptance disagree until the kit gap in I1 lands. findings.source: docs/trace/ui/U8/verdicts/A1-reviewer.json R1, R2 (P1), R3, R4 (P2); docs/trace/ui/U8/verdicts/A1-security.json (PASS; note 58 is the same publish race as R1)
findings.symptom: Reviewer R1, and the security verdict's note at A1-security.json:58 (one cause, two reports). Layer note: this is the ui client layer, not the C# API; 'api' follows the W3 A1/I5 convention. the request log can show an exchange with a status but no response body. That breaks WB-7 ('the exact request and response') and HONEST-1. It also drops the selling POST from the policy view's sale match, because that match reads responseBody (src/web/app/workbench/policy/PolicyView.tsx:340).
findings.cause: publish() treats an exchange as settled when its status is non-null and then reuses that object for good (src/web/app/workbench/browser.ts:25). But loggingFetch settles an entry in three steps with an await in the middle. It sets status (src/web/app/data/api.ts:440) and headers (:441), then awaits response.clone().text() before it sets responseBody (:442). A publish() from another request, on its send (browser.ts:32) or its finally (:36), can land in that await. When it does, it takes a shallow copy holding status and headers but responseBody null. The entry's own final publish then keeps that stale copy (browser.ts:25), so the body never reaches any snapshot. The status test is the wrong marker of 'settled': settled has to mean the body has been read too. The test missed it because wb-7-log-growth.test.tsx:37 awaits each fetch in turn, so no publish ever falls inside another exchange's body read. Recurrence: this is a new fingerprint, but attempt 1's own route introduced it (diff.patch:9784-9788, green 8148181). That route was the fix for W3 A4 I9 (W4|src/web/app/workbench/browser.ts|unbounded-log-full-copy-per-publish). The fix removed the per-publish copy and keyed reuse on a field that is set before the entry is complete. So I9's cause is closed, and its fix opened this one.
findings.fixDirection: count an exchange as settled for reuse only once every field loggingFetch writes is in place, the body included. Or make loggingFetch complete the entry in one step after the body read. Then add a test with two exchanges in flight at once.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the global fetch stubbed so that exchange A's response body is a stream the test holds open, and exchange B's answers at once. When A is sent and has its status, B is sent and answered while A's body is still unread, and then A's body is released and A settles. Then the request log the page reads holds A with its status and with responseBody equal to the exact text released, and the policy view's sale match would find A's reference in it. (tests/web/unit/client/wb-7-log-concurrent.test.tsx, beside wb-7-log-growth.test.tsx, WB-7 · prefix)

findings.source: docs/trace/ui/U8/verdicts/A1-reviewer.json R1, R2 (P1), R3, R4 (P2); docs/trace/ui/U8/verdicts/A1-security.json (PASS; note 58 is the same publish race as R1)
findings.symptom: Reviewer R2. Layer note: ui screen layer, with 'api' per the convention. acceptance line 9b (docs/plans/active/ui.dag.yaml:462) wants the 'amount null' renewal explained or fixed in RenewPolicy. The node's only trace of it is gate.red's 'amount-null not reproducible' (docs/trace/ui/U8/loop.jsonl:3), and the diff doesn't touch the amount path. Cause, which is deterministic and not intermittent: submit sends Number(amount) with no check (src/web/app/workbench/renew/RenewPolicy.tsx:91). The field is the kit MoneyInput, a free text input that parses nothing on entry (src/web/kit/primitives/money-input/MoneyInput.tsx:8-9, :19). So any text Number() can't read, such as '12,50', '£100' or a doubled default like '100.00100.00', becomes NaN. postJson's JSON.stringify (src/web/app/data/api.ts:413) then writes NaN as null. RenewalRequest.amount is typed number (api.ts:394), so the page can't send the typed text as it was typed. That conflicts with MoneyInput's own contract that 'the rules are the API's'. An empty field also goes out as 0, a value nobody typed (HONEST-1). What put non-numeric text in the field during W3's single failing run is still unknown. The mechanism that turns any such text into null is the line above, and it can be reproduced at will. Recurrence: this was carried from W3 A4 I6 (WB-5|tests/web/e2e/W3/wb-5.spec.ts|cheque-test-types-before-read-amount-null-intermittent). Attempt 1 fixed that fingerprint's test half (9a, met per the reviewer's note). It treated the code half as 'not reproducible' because it looked for the intermittent trigger and didn't explain the deterministic conversion I6 named. The code-side cause gets its own fingerprint here, so this is not a repeat of I6's.
findings.fixDirection: RenewPolicy must stop sending an invented null or 0 for an amount nobody gave. Either the form refuses a non-numeric or empty amount before sending and says why, or the client sends the typed text exactly so the API's own 400 answers it. The choice and its reason go into the trail, which explains line 9b as well as fixing it. David may want to rule between the two, since one adds a check in the UI.
findings.suggestedTest: Given the renew screen after the policy read has answered, with a stub fetch. When the person replaces the amount with 'abc', or clears it, and presses Renew policy. Then no request body {"amount":null} or {"amount":0} is sent: either no POST goes out and the field says why, or the POST body carries the text as typed. (tests/web/unit/screens/wb-5-renew-amount.test.tsx, WB-5 · prefix)

findings.source: docs/trace/ui/U9/verdicts/A1-reviewer.json R1, R2, R5; docs/trace/ui/U9/verdicts/A1-security.json S1
findings.symptom: Deploy_<env> ships only the App Service zip.
findings.cause: the attempt-1 builder stopped at its 25-minute box (gate.write detail in docs/trace/ui/U9/packet/gates.jsonl:1: 'Builder stopped at its 25m box after committing 7910201, 8f23c27') before writing the web deploy. The deploy steps at infrastructure/pipelines/stage-template.yml:73-160 are infra (75-97), migrations (116-125), DB grant (130-141), az webapp deploy (143-154) and the /health/ready curl (156-160). No step reads the Static Web App deployment token from the resource, deploys the `web` artifact (published at infrastructure/pipelines/azure-pipelines.yml:122-124) with the SWA CLI, or smoke-tests the site root. Acceptance line 8 asks for the web build 'before the Static Web Apps deploy', line 4 for 'a web build and deploy stage', and line 5 for 'deployment token from the resource, never in params'. The check passed anyway because infrastructure/pipelines/check-pipeline.py has no assertion on the deploy job for a Static Web App deploy, a token read or a site smoke test (the Web-stage needles at 52-53 cover only the build side). That is the reviewer's R6, already deferred. Not verified here: deployment jobs auto-download the current pipeline's artifacts, as the job already uses `drop` at stage-template.yml:68-69 without a download step, so the missing piece is the deploy, token and smoke steps, not necessarily a download step.
findings.fixDirection: in the deploy job, after the app deploy, add a step on the ARM connection that reads the token from the site named by $(webSiteName) into a masked secret variable, a step that deploys $(Pipeline.Workspace)/web with a pinned SWA CLI with the token passed through the step's environment (never a parameter or variable group), and a curl --fail of https://$(webHostName)/. Constraints: check-pipeline.py:120-121 requires the last step to curl /health/ready, so either the site smoke test joins that last step or that assertion is widened (in scope). The pipeline.schema.json task branch (136-144, additionalProperties false) has no `env`, so a task step carrying the token needs that branch widened, or the token must go through a script step, whose branch already allows `env` (118).
findings.suggestedTest: Given infrastructure/pipelines/stage-template.yml as at HEAD, When python -I infrastructure/pipelines/check-pipeline.py runs with new assertions that the deployment job has a step running 'az staticwebapp secrets list' that emits a secret (issecret=true) variable, a step that deploys the 'web' artifact path with a version-pinned SWA CLI taking the token only through env, and a curl --fail of https://$(webHostName)/, Then it exits 1 at HEAD and 0 once the steps exist (check-pipeline.py, the pipeline schema check)

findings.source: gate.green ok:false in docs/trace/bug-002/N1/loop.jsonl, head 35122e4b (run 1 392/393: data-1-trace-on-start.test.ts 'DATA-1 · a compile that fails is reported in the console, naming each problem, and no trace.json is served' failed at :138; runs 2 and 3 passed 393/393)
findings.symptom: in the failing run's log, the captured output has 'trace compile failed: docs/trace/build/F1/activity.jsonl:2 ...' and then 'Local: http://localhost:51476/', but not the loop.jsonl:3 line. So :137 passed and :138 failed.
findings.cause: the test reads the dev server's stdout and stderr into one string (data-1-trace-on-start.test.ts:73-74). startVite resolves as soon as 'Local:' turns up on either stream (:75-90), and the test reads that string only once, at :136. Two pipes have no ordering between them, so a stderr chunk the child wrote before the stdout 'Local:' line can still be read after it. The orchestrator's hypothesis is confirmed, with one correction. Inside the dev server, log.error never races printUrls: the order is fixed. vite.config.ts:42-46 logs every problem synchronously in the 'close' handler and then calls done(). printUrls only runs in a later microtask, through compiled.then (vite.config.ts:50). Vite's logger sends 'error' to console.error, which is stderr, and 'info' (the Local: line) to console.log, which is stdout (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:14783,14797). The race is in the test process reading the two pipes. The product side is complete and in order. The compiler writes each problem with console.error and sets process.exitCode rather than calling process.exit, so no output is cut off (compiler/index.ts:437-438). The plugin collects stderr until 'close', which fires only after the child's stdio has ended (vite.config.ts:40-42), so `problems` holds both lines. The log also shows the plugin logged the first of the two lines, and the second is written right after it in the same synchronous loop (:44). Missing it can only be a read-timing gap, not a logging gap. The same read-once-at-'Local:' pattern is at data-1-first-run.test.ts:262-265 (the preview branch). It doesn't run at HEAD: traceOnStart never applies under preview (vite.config.ts:35), so the test returns at :256. I've merged it into this finding, on purpose, because it has the same cause. Not the cause: the 'Re-optimizing dependencies because vite config has changed' line. It comes from the shared cacheDir (vite.config.ts:78) seen through the node_modules junction. It adds startup time but doesn't affect which problem lines get captured.
findings.fixDirection: (product code unchanged, assertions unchanged) after 'Local:' appears, the test should wait, within a deadline, until the captured output names every expected problem (or the server exits), and only then run the same two toContain assertions. The waitFor helper in data-1-first-run.test.ts:90-109 already does this. Apply the same to the dormant preview branch. Don't move the compile problems to stdout, and don't drop or relax the loop.jsonl:3 assertion. Logging all problems in one log.error call would make the race rarer, but it wouldn't remove the cross-pipe ordering gap.
findings.untestableReason: The defect is in the test's own observation, not in product behaviour. The dev server writes both problem lines to stderr before 'Local:' goes to stdout on every run (vite.config.ts:42-50). Which order the test process reads the two pipes in is up to the OS pipe reads and the libuv event loop, and no product-facing test can force it. So no test fails reliably on this HEAD. The fix is proved by the existing DATA-1 test, with its assertions unchanged, passing across repeated gate runs.

findings.source: A2: docs/trace/bug-002/N1/verdicts/A2-reviewer.json R1, R2, R3, R4, R5; docs/trace/bug-002/N1/verdicts/A2-security.json S1 (investigation inv-010)
findings.symptom: UI layer: loader (app/data/trace.ts and app/shell). The schema's 'api' is the nearest allowed value. F5 on 'API and web' opens Docket while the trail is still compiling, and the page stays on 'Could not load · trace.json could not be read (HTTP 503)' until someone reloads it by hand. CAUSE: listen-first (35122e4b) added a short-lived server state, 503 'The trail is compiling; try again in a moment.' (vite.config.ts:60-62). The only reader of /trace.json treats every non-2xx answer as final and asks only once. readJson turns any non-ok answer into '<path> could not be read (HTTP n)' and drops the body (app/data/trace.ts:245-246). loadTrace then returns state 'error' (trace.ts:264-265). useTraceFile calls loadTrace once, on mount, and never asks again (app/shell/Frame.tsx:41-53). So DataNotice draws 'Could not load' (app/shell/DataNotice.tsx:13-16). DATA-1 says 'the SPA reads only that file', and HEAD's SPA gives up on that file before it exists. TRIGGER, NOT CAUSE: Vite 8 opens the browser inside listen() (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:24964). The CLI calls listen and then printUrls (node_modules/vite/dist/node/cli.js:725, :732). So holding back printUrls (vite.config.ts:49-50) holds back the 'Local:' line but not the browser, and launch.json:10 passes --open. On base the compile ran in the config hook, before listen (packet/diff.patch:9839-9844), so this window did not exist. THE HYPOTHESIS HOLDS ON ALL THREE COUNTS: Vite opens on listen, the shell does not retry a 503, and no test opens the page during the compile. The DATA-1 toolchain tests ask /trace.json with Node's fetch only (data-1-first-run.test.ts:198-227). The launch-path test removes --open (:182). Every e2e runs on build plus preview (playwright.config.ts:16), where there is no 503 window. The loader's unit tests have no 503 case (data-1.test.ts:39-109). RECURRENCE: no. This is a new fingerprint; A1/I1 was the stdout/stderr read race. The earlier route didn't prevent it because inv-009's recommendation ('let Vite listen first and answer /trace.json compiling', inv-009.plan.md:71) and N1's acceptance line 2 (bug-002.dag.yaml:28) specify only what the server answers. Yet inv-009 I3 had already recorded that Vite opens the browser once it is listening (inv-009.plan.md:39). The A1 investigation was scoped to the gate flake. FIX DIRECTIONS: (b) on its own does not remove the cause. Any page load inside the window still lands on the final error: an open tab's Vite client reloads as soon as the restarted server answers its ping (node_modules/vite/dist/client/client.mjs:1083-1088), which under listen-first is before the compile ends, as on a second F5 with the tab left open. The Edge configuration (launch.json:12-18), a manual open and a refresh do the same. (b) would also need a second override of Vite's lifecycle, like the printUrls override. (a) removes the cause on every path with the least new behaviour. While the server says it is compiling, the loader keeps the state it already has for 'trace.json is being read' (DataNotice.tsx:6-11), with no new component, and asks again until the file is ready or the compile has failed. Two constraints: the 'did not compile' 503 and the 404 must stay final after one request (data-1.test.ts:88-95), and production has no compiling state. So the re-ask must key on the compiling answer, not on status 503 alone. Today the two 503s differ only in their prose (vite.config.ts:62), as I5 notes. (c) adds (b)'s lifecycle override on top of (a) for a cosmetic gain only. Recommend (a).
findings.suggestedTest: First to fail on this HEAD (data-1.test.ts, unit/data). Given a fetch that answers trace.json with 503 and the body 'The trail is compiling; try again in a moment.' twice, and then serves the compiled complete fixture, When loadTrace settles, Then its state is ready with the fixture's trace, and trace.json was requested three times. On HEAD it settles as 'error' with 'trace.json could not be read (HTTP 503)' after one request. Guard in the same file: Given a 503 with 'The trail did not compile; see the console of the dev server.', Then the state is error after exactly one request. End-to-end proof, the case no test covers today: Given the dev server started on the complete trail plus 300 commits, When a Playwright page opens / before the compile ends, Then the overview draws the trail without a reload and never shows 'Could not load'.

findings.cause: vite.config.ts:53 runs decodeURIComponent on every request URL before the path filter at :54. It throws URIError on a malformed escape, and connect turns the throw into a 500. Vite's own transform middleware handles the same input by warning and calling next() (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:20351-20356), so the plugin overrides Vite's policy for every path. This node introduced the decode: base read the raw path (packet/diff.patch:9874-9875). It is needed only by the traversal guard for /trace.json and /trace/* (vite.config.ts:55-56). This finding deliberately covers both R3 and the decode half of S1: same line, same cause. S1's EISDIR half has its own cause (I4). RECURRENCE: no. FIX DIRECTION: decide whether the request is for /trace.json or /trace/* before decoding, decode only for those, and answer a malformed escape there with a 4xx instead of throwing.

findings.cause: RecordClaim.tsx:255-257 moves the drawer out of the record region into a new tagged section. The signed-off screen has 4 regions and puts the drawer inside 'record claim, busy while the request and the two quotes run' (docs/ui/screens/wb-claim/screen.json:43-46, components button, spinner, inspector-drawer; populated.html:53-71, below the button and note, inside a `div.s-dock`). The overlap the move tried to fix comes from the kit drawer being `position: sticky; bottom: 0` (InspectorDrawer.module.css:2-5). Its sticky range is its parent, which was the whole record section, so it could ride up over the Record button in that same section. Origin: the plan's green direction 'mounted at form level' (bug-002.dag.yaml:73) was read as 'a region of its own'. Direction: put the drawer back inside the BUSY-1 region after the button and note, wrapped in the screen's own dock element. The kit drawer is position: sticky; bottom: 0 (InspectorDrawer.module.css:2-5), so its sticky range is that whole section. By sticky positioning, in a real browser the drawer covers the h2 for every scroll where the window's bottom falls between the section's top and the section's top plus the h2, the gap and the drawer's height. That's a band of several hundred px. I couldn't measure this in a browser, because I only have read access; the test below measures it. findings.symptom: Layer: the Docket workbench drawer adapter. The schema has no web layer, so 'api' marks the screen that calls the API, as in A1 and A2. (R1) the requests drawer shows money tokens the API never sent: 803.40 shows as 803.4, 500.00 as 500, and a 0.00 refund as 0. The orchestrator's node check shows the same.
findings.cause: forDisplay at RequestsDrawer.tsx:13 indents a JSON body by sending it through JSON.parse and then JSON.stringify. That turns every JSON number into a JS double and writes it back in the shortest form, so the trailing zeros are lost. Both the request (:21) and the response (:22) go through it. The token is exact on the wire, because the API writes every decimal raw with at least two places (TwoDecimalPlacesConverter.cs:7-9, :16-17, :19-29). The log keeps it exact too, because loggingFetch stores response.clone().text() unchanged (api.ts:442-445). The kit drawer prints request.exchange as text unchanged (kit InspectorDrawer.tsx:181-188). So the only change happens at RequestsDrawer.tsx:13. The comment at :10, 'indented for reading', describes a whitespace-only change that the code doesn't make. Rule: WB-7, 'The exact request and response of every action' (docs/ui-requirements.md:174). A re-serialised body is not the exact response. The kit already sets the contract this breaks. JsonViewer re-indents 'never re-parsed into other numbers, so "615.40" stays "615.40"' (JsonViewer.tsx:7). It does this with a token-copying walk over the raw text (:23-67), and parses only to check the text is valid (:69-76). The /requests page uses it (RequestLogPage.tsx:75), so the drawer is the one place that goes the other way. That indent helper isn't exported from the kit barrel (kit/patterns/json-viewer/index.ts:1-2), and a build node may not change the kit. Not a recurrence: forDisplay came in with this node's A1 I13 indent work, and no earlier fingerprint names it. Direction: the drawer has to indent the received text by changing whitespace only, copying every token (numbers, strings, literals) character for character, and use JSON parsing only to decide whether a body is JSON. A body that isn't JSON stays exactly as received, as now. The wire text in the log stays untouched. Same cause as I2, from the test side: I2 explains why no test caught this one.
