findings.symptom: Layer: the Docket workbench screen. The schema's enum has no web layer, so 'api' marks the screen that calls the API, as in N2's A1 and A2. in the wb-renew shots re-taken at 06d68df4, the open requests drawer lies over the page's content. In api-unreachable-1440-light.png (which I opened) the drawer's top edge sits under the 'Renewal amount' hint and covers the amount input and all of section 2, including the 'The API did not answer' banner. A blank band then shows between section 4 and the footer. QA step 16 records the same at 390 (header, timeline, violations).
findings.cause: RenewPolicy.tsx:233 mounts <RequestsDrawer /> as a direct child of the form. The form is the .s-wb-page grid (RenewPolicy.tsx:112; workbench.css:2-7), and the kit drawer is position: sticky; bottom: 0 (InspectorDrawer.module.css:1-5). Its sticky range is therefore the whole form, sections 1 to 4, so whenever its normal place is below the window's bottom it rides up, as far as the form's top, over whatever is on screen. A full-page capture is the extreme case, which is why the shot shows it parked over sections 1 and 2 and leaves an empty band where it belongs. Why it appears now: before N2 the drawer stayed closed on renew, so only its thin bar rode over the content. N2 made RequestsDrawer open whenever the log grows (RequestsDrawer.tsx:84-88), and renew's on-open read GET /policies/{ref} (RenewPolicy.tsx:73-86) grows the log. So the drawer is open, body and all, on every renew state, the unreachable one included. Claim, cancel and sell don't do this: each wraps the drawer in the layout-only .s-wb-dock (RecordClaim.tsx:254-256, CancelPolicy.tsx:331-332, SellPolicy.tsx:417-418; workbench.css:25-29), whose box is exactly the drawer's, so the drawer stays in flow (N2 A1 I3, A2 I1). Renew has no dock. Origin: N2's A1 I4 directed 'mount the drawer untagged, as before N2' to remove a 5th parity region, and so restored the bare mount without giving it a sticky range of its own. The signed-off wb-renew puts the drawer in the frame after main, closed, with 0 requests (populated.html:61; screen.json:64 'in the frame'). Its BUSY-1 region's components are only button and spinner (screen.json:42-46), so the claim fix (the drawer inside the BUSY-1 region) does not carry over as it stands. HONEST-1: nothing is invented here. HONEST-1's harm is that the drawer hides the only true account of the failure (the unreachable banner, RenewPolicy.tsx:191-201), while the header above says 'Nothing yet. The policy was not read.' The rule broken is WB-7's inspector layout, not HONEST-1's 'no invented data'. Not a recurrence of a fingerprint: it is the same sticky mechanism as N2 inv-011 I1 (sell), in a fourth file. Direction: give renew's drawer a sticky range of its own box, a layout-only dock with no data-region or data-req, after section 4, so the 4 signed-off regions and their order stay as parity expects. The drawer is then never over sections 1 to 4 and the page ends at the footer. This departs from the signed-off 'in the frame, after main' placement, the same kind of layout departure as sell's dock, so show it at the next pause. Then re-shoot wb-renew's baselines. The PNGs re-taken at 06d68df4 have the overlap in them, so the regression spec now passes against the defect, and those baselines must not be signed.

findings.symptom: the A1/I8 check says the question bank has 7 rows, but the spec says "30 questions" (api-guide.spec.md:11) and "Met at 30" (api-guide.spec.md:235). The spec is right: it has 16 developer rows, DQ1-DQ16 (api-guide.spec.md:17-32), and 14 servicer rows, SQ1-SQ14 (api-guide.spec.md:38-51), which makes 30. The cause is in the check. check.test.mjs:179 counts rows with the pattern `^\| [ADU]\d+ \|` over the whole spec. That pattern matches the F7-era IDs A1-A10, D1-D10 and U1-U10 (see docs/trace/build/F7/findings/A1.md:69). It doesn't match the DQ/SQ IDs that commit 6f2e8efc introduced when it regrouped the bank by persona, as the plan requires (feat-001.plan.md:41). Because the pattern isn't limited to §1, it instead counts the 7 diagram rows D1-D7 (api-guide.spec.md:158-164). So 7 is the diagram count, not a question count, and the check fails a correct spec. The receipts-path half of the same test passes (api-guide.spec.md:217 names docs/guides/api/receipts.md, which exists).
findings.fixDirection: change the check, not the spec. It should count only the question-bank rows in §1, under the persona-grouped DQ/SQ IDs. Diagram rows and other tables must not be counted. Every stated count must still equal the real row count, and the receipts-path assertion stays as it is. Don't change the spec's 30. Lowering it to 7 would make a correct spec wrong just to satisfy a broken check. Is the failing check the red test? No. It fails for the wrong reason (it miscounts), so it shows the check is broken, not the spec. Once the check is fixed, it acts as the regression check for the stated count (it should pass on the spec at 6f2e8efc). The check's own red evidence is this gate receipt: it shows the old pattern returning 7 on a 30-row bank.

findings.symptom: (R1) from 2026-10-26 onwards, a reader following the servicer journey gets 422 SELL-2 on the GUIDE-002 sale, and the later GUIDE-002 steps then fail too.
findings.cause: every request in the journey uses a fixed date that only works on the capture day, and the guide never tells the reader to move them. The commands are recorded as fixed strings in run-receipts.sh:90-109: C01 starts 2026-11-01, C03 and C05 use 2026-11-10, C08 starts 2026-10-25, F08 uses 2026-10-24, C09 uses 2026-10-25 and F06 uses 2026-10-26. The script comment at run-receipts.sh:5-6 admits 'the dates in the commands below only fit that day'. The guide copies them as they are (index.html:806, :840, :982). The only explanation is the summary at index.html:760, which says 'today is 2026-10-25' but never tells the reader to move the dates to their own today. The only hint is the troubleshooting row at index.html:1234. This breaks LRN-5 ('the exact command ... and what you should see') and feat-001.dag.yaml:33 ('A reader follows one persona journey in a PDF against the running app and reaches each step's shown result'). SELL-2 accepts a start date only from today to today + 60 (index.html:103). So C08 fails from 2026-10-26, C01 fails after 2026-11-01, the CANCEL-3 and COULD-2a examples (F08, F06) stop showing what they are meant to show, and C09's claim date stops being today. A second effect: the outputs shown (daysUsed, refundAmount at index.html:919, :927, :979, quotedOn, and the SELL-2 window detail at :828) are tied to 2026-10-25. Even dates moved correctly reproduce them only if every date moves by the same offset, and the guide doesn't say which values will then differ. The symptom is the 422 on a later day; the cause is fixed capture-day dates with no instruction to move them.
findings.fixDirection: make each servicer-journey date relative to the reader's own today, either by a clear instruction with the offsets from today or by dates the reader's shell works out. Keep the commands receipted, since checks A1/I1 and A1/I4 in check.test.mjs:101-111 and :156-163 require the guide's command text to match a receipts.md Command line. Say plainly which shown values (dates, days and refund amounts, quotedOn) will differ from the reader's run and why. Carried from F7 A2 R4 and A2.2 R4 (other plans); this is the first fix attempt on this node.
